question: A 2-year-old child on the ward who is fed through a nasogastric tube coughs and becomes flushed during the morning feed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Record the cough in the chart and repeat the feed after an hour
option_2: Give the rest of the feed slowly so that the child is NOT left hungry
option_3: Turn the child on to the back and continue the feed as ordered
option_4: Stop the feed at once, sit the child up and check the tube and the chest
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Stop the feed at once, sit the child up and check the tube and the chest

Clinical Rationale: A cough with flushing during a nasogastric feed suggests that the feed is entering the lungs, so the feed is stopped at once, the child is sat up and the tube and the chest are checked.

Key Clue: 2-year-old child fed through a nasogastric tube who coughs and becomes flushed during a feed

Priority Principle: Safety / Tube feed

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting an hour allows a feed in the lungs to cause infection; (b) The rest of the feed will enter the lungs of a child who is coughing; (c) A feed given on the back lets the milk flow the wrong way.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the child's hunger seems a reason to finish the feed.

5-Second Recall: Tube feed me khansi aur laal chehra = feed band karo, baithao, tube check karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A cough during a tube feed is treated first as a tube in the wrong place.

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward is receiving a drug through an intravenous pump, and the nurse must add a second drug on a fresh order. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Check the order, the site of the line and the flow before the second drug is given
option_2: Stop the pump and push the second drug into the same line at once
option_3: Add the second drug to the bottle of the FIRST drug and start the pump
option_4: Ask the man to keep his arm still and continue the drug round
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check the order, the site of the line and the flow before the second drug is given

Clinical Rationale: The order, the site of the line and the flow are checked before a second drug is added, so that the two drugs are NOT mixed and the arm is NOT harmed.

Key Clue: a drug running into the vein by a pump and a fresh order for a second drug

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Line and pump

Why Not Others: (b) A push into the same line may not be safe with the other drug; (c) A second drug added to the first bottle gives an unknown strength; (d) Continuing the drug round does not check the line for the second drug.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a push seems the quick way to give a fresh order.

5-Second Recall: Doosri dawa se pehle order, site aur flow check karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every new drug on a line needs the order, the site and the flow checked.

question: A 70-year-old man on the ward who has had a urinary catheter for three days now has a fever of 38.5 degrees Celsius, cloudy urine and suprapubic pain. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Remove the catheter at once and ask the man to pass urine himself
option_2: Inspect the catheter, send the urine for testing and inform the doctor
option_3: Apply a warm pack to the lower abdomen and note the colour of the urine
option_4: Wash the catheter with saline and continue the drainage
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Inspect the catheter, send the urine for testing and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A fever with cloudy urine and suprapubic pain in a man with a catheter points to a catheter-associated infection, so the catheter is inspected, the urine is sent for testing and the doctor is informed.

Key Clue: 70-year-old man with a urinary catheter for three days, a fever of 38.5 and cloudy urine with suprapubic pain

Priority Principle: Infection / Urinary catheter

Why Not Others: (a) Removing the catheter without an order leaves the man with a full bladder; (c) A warm pack and a note leave the infection without a test; (d) Washing the catheter pushes the germs up into the bladder.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a catheter that stays seems the cause that must be removed.

5-Second Recall: Catheter, bukhar aur gandha peshaab = urine test aur doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A urine sample is taken before an antibiotic is given for a bladder infection.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 50-year-old man on the ward who has a tracheostomy tube makes a whistling sound with each breath and is restless with a fast pulse. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the man to take deep breaths and cough out the plug
option_2: Place a moist cloth over the opening of the tube at once
option_3: Suction the tube with a sterile catheter and give oxygen
option_4: Record the whistling sound in the chart and call the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Suction the tube with a sterile catheter and give oxygen

Clinical Rationale: A whistling sound with restlessness in a man with a tracheostomy points to a mucus plug, so the tube is suctioned with a sterile catheter and oxygen is given.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man with a tracheostomy, a whistling sound with each breath and restlessness

Priority Principle: ABC / Airway

Why Not Others: (a) A cough cannot clear a plug that is stuck in the tube; (b) A moist cloth over the opening keeps air out of the tube; (d) A note alone leaves the airway blocked.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a note in the chart seems the careful FIRST step.

5-Second Recall: Tracheostomy me seeti ki awaaz = sucker se saaf karo, oxygen do.

PNC Exam Pearl: A whistle with restlessness in a tracheostomy is a plug until proved otherwise.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse checks the flow meter of the oxygen running into a 65-year-old man on the ward with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and finds the ball at 8 litres per minute, while the order is for 2 litres per minute. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Leave the flow as it is because more oxygen helps a breathless man
option_2: Turn the flow down to the ordered rate and observe the man's breathing
option_3: Remove the mask from the man's face and call the doctor
option_4: Record the meter reading and continue the ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Turn the flow down to the ordered rate and observe the man's breathing

Clinical Rationale: A flow of 8 litres in a man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease retains carbon dioxide, so the flow is turned down to the ordered rate at once.

Key Clue: oxygen flow meter at 8 litres per minute for a 65-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and an order for 2 litres

Priority Principle: ABC / Oxygen flow

Why Not Others: (a) A high flow in a man of this kind removes his drive to breathe; (c) Removing the mask leaves the man without the ordered oxygen; (d) A note of the reading leaves the wrong flow running.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because more oxygen seems safer for a breathless man.

5-Second Recall: COPD wale client me oxygen 8 litre nahi - order ke hisaab se kam karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The ordered flow of oxygen is set before anything else on the round.

question: A nurse reads the label of an intravenous bag running into a 55-year-old woman on the ward and finds a strength that is four times the doctor's order. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Run the bag slowly so that the strength does NOT harm the woman
option_2: Let the bag run but note the strength in the woman's chart
option_3: Stop the flow at once, keep the vein open with saline and inform the doctor
option_4: Remove the bag and hang a fresh bag of the same drug from the shelf
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stop the flow at once, keep the vein open with saline and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A bag with four times the ordered strength is stopped at once, the vein is kept open with saline and the doctor is informed, so that no extra drug enters the woman.

Key Clue: intravenous bag for a 55-year-old woman with a strength four times the doctor's order

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Drug strength

Why Not Others: (a) A slow rate of a strong bag still gives too much of the drug; (b) A note does not stop the strong drug from entering the vein; (d) A fresh bag of the same drug may be mixed up in the same way.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a slow rate seems the safe way to give a strong drug.

5-Second Recall: Order se chaar guna strength = flow band, saline se line khuli rakho, doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: The strength on the label is read against the order before the flow is left running.

question: A nurse checks the monitor of a 60-year-old woman on the ward and sees a heart rate of 36 per minute, and the woman says that she feels giddy. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Leave the woman until the round and record the monitor reading
option_2: Give a drug for the slow rate without a doctor's order
option_3: Change the monitor leads because the reading must be wrong
option_4: Feel the woman's pulse by hand and look at her condition
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Feel the woman's pulse by hand and look at her condition

Clinical Rationale: A slow rate on the monitor with giddiness is checked against the woman's pulse by hand, because the machine may show a false rate and the woman is the one who decides her care.

Key Clue: monitor showing a heart rate of 36 per minute in a 60-year-old woman who feels giddy

Priority Principle: ABC / Slow heart rate

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for the round leaves a slow rate without care; (b) A drug for the rate is given only on the doctor's order; (c) Fresh leads before the woman's pulse put the machine before the client.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a wrong machine seems the FIRST thing to set right.

5-Second Recall: Monitor 36 aur chakkar = pehle haath se nadi dekho, phir doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The machine is checked against the client and not the client against the machine.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 60-year-old woman on the ward has an intravenous drip, and the nurse finds the bottle empty with blood in the line up to the cannula. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Close the clamp of the line at once and remove the line
option_2: Take the bottle down and shake the line to bring the blood back
option_3: Open the clamp wide and run saline into the line
option_4: Record the empty bottle in the chart and hang the next bottle
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Close the clamp of the line at once and remove the line

Clinical Rationale: A line with blood in it from an empty bottle is closed at once and removed, so that no air enters the woman's vein.

Key Clue: empty drip bottle with blood in the line up to the cannula in the arm of a 60-year-old woman

Priority Principle: Safety / Drip line

Why Not Others: (b) Shaking the line does not take the blood out of the cannula; (c) A wide clamp pushes blood and air into the vein; (d) The next bottle is hung after the line is closed and the air kept out.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because more fluid seems the way to push the blood back.

5-Second Recall: Bottle khaali aur line me khoon = clamp turant band karo, line nikaalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The clamp is closed before the bottle is touched.

question: A 40-year-old man on the ward who is to have electroconvulsive therapy in the morning has eaten the ward breakfast. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Inform the doctor and the team at once so that the treatment is postponed
option_2: Continue with the treatment because the man has taken only a light meal
option_3: Give the man a drink of water and take him to the treatment room
option_4: Note the meal in the chart and give the pre-treatment drugs as ordered
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Inform the doctor and the team at once so that the treatment is postponed

Clinical Rationale: Electroconvulsive therapy needs an empty stomach, so the meal is reported to the doctor and the team at once and the treatment is postponed.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man due for electroconvulsive therapy who has eaten the ward breakfast

Priority Principle: Safety / Electroconvulsive therapy

Why Not Others: (b) A light meal in the stomach causes vomiting into the airway during this treatment; (c) Water is withheld before the treatment and the meal is the fault; (d) The pre-treatment drugs are given after the fault is reported to the team.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a light meal seems a small matter for the treatment.

5-Second Recall: Machine wale ilaaj se pehle khana nahi - khana khaya to team ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The stomach is kept empty before a treatment given with the machine.

question: A nurse at a sub-centre must reconstitute the measles vaccine with the diluent for the child who comes to the OPD at the morning session. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Mix the powder with the water of the pump and use it for the session
option_2: Check the label on the vial and mix it with the diluent supplied with it
option_3: Mix the whole powder and keep the fluid in the cold box for the week
option_4: Mix the powder with saline so that the child feels less pain
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check the label on the vial and mix it with the diluent supplied with it

Clinical Rationale: The label on the vial is checked and the powder is mixed with the diluent supplied with it, and the reconstituted vaccine is used within the set hour.

Key Clue: measles vaccine to be reconstituted for the session at the sub-centre

Priority Principle: Cold chain / Vaccine reconstitution

Why Not Others: (a) Pump water is not clean for a vaccine that enters the body; (c) A reconstituted vaccine kept for days has lost its potency; (d) Saline is not the diluent of the vaccine and harms its potency.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because keeping the fluid seems a saving of the vaccine.

5-Second Recall: Measles vaccine sirf apne diluent se, aur ghante ke andar use karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A vaccine mixed with the wrong fluid is discarded.

question: A nurse must insert a nasogastric tube for a feed in a 50-year-old man on the ward who is awake and cooperative. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Instil 20 mL of water down the tube to confirm that it is in the stomach
option_2: Ask the man to swallow as the tube is pushed quickly through the nose
option_3: Check the order, explain the procedure to the man and position him sitting up with the head of the bed raised
option_4: Tape the tube to the nose before confirming its position in the stomach
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Check the order, explain the procedure to the man and position him sitting up with the head of the bed raised

Clinical Rationale: The order is checked, the procedure is explained and the man is positioned sitting up with the head of the bed raised before the tube is passed, so that he is prepared and the tube passes smoothly.

Key Clue: nasogastric tube to be inserted for a feed in a 50-year-old man who is awake

Priority Principle: Procedure / Nasogastric tube

Why Not Others: (a) Water is not instilled to confirm the position of the tube; (b) A fast push causes distress and may injure the nasal passage; (d) The tube is taped only after its position in the stomach is confirmed.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a fast pass seems the way to shorten the discomfort.

5-Second Recall: Tube se pehle client ko samjhao aur baithao, phir naapo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The client is prepared and positioned before the tube is passed.

question: A nurse must collect a urine specimen for culture from a 45-year-old woman on the ward who already has a urinary catheter. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Empty the bag into a pot and send the pot to the laboratory
option_2: Collect the urine from the drainage bag hanging below the bed
option_3: Remove the catheter and ask the woman to pass urine into a pot
option_4: Clean the sampling port and draw the urine with a sterile syringe
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Clean the sampling port and draw the urine with a sterile syringe

Clinical Rationale: The sampling port is cleaned and the urine is drawn with a sterile syringe, because the urine in the bag has been standing and contains other germs.

Key Clue: urine for culture from the catheter of a 45-year-old woman

Priority Principle: Procedure / Urine specimen

Why Not Others: (a) Bag urine mixed with old urine gives a wrong report; (b) The urine in the bag has been standing and is not fresh bladder urine; (c) The catheter is removed only on the doctor's order.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the bag seems the pot that holds the urine.

5-Second Recall: Culture ke liye urine catheter ke chhote darwaze se, bag se nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: A culture specimen is taken fresh from the bladder and not from the bag.

question: A nurse is giving an intramuscular injection to a 45-year-old woman on the ward and, on pulling back the plunger, dark blood appears in the barrel. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Withdraw the needle, press the site and choose a fresh site and a fresh needle
option_2: Push the drug slowly into the muscle with the blood in the barrel
option_3: Pull the plunger back again and push the drug in when no blood appears
option_4: Continue at the same site and give the drug after a fresh swab
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Withdraw the needle, press the site and choose a fresh site and a fresh needle

Clinical Rationale: Blood in the barrel means that the needle is in a vessel, so the needle is withdrawn, the site is pressed and a fresh site with a fresh needle is chosen.

Key Clue: dark blood in the barrel while giving an intramuscular injection to a 45-year-old woman

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Injection site

Why Not Others: (b) A drug pushed into a vessel acts at once and harms the woman; (c) The needle that has drawn blood is withdrawn and never used again; (d) A fresh swab does not move the needle out of the vessel.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a second pull seems the careful check of the site.

5-Second Recall: Barrel me khoon = sui nikaalo, nayi jagah aur nayi sui lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A needle that draws blood is withdrawn at once and never used again.

question: A 40-year-old man on the ward who has a chest drain after surgery now has sudden shortness of breath, and his oxygen saturation on the finger has fallen to 88 per cent. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clamp the drain at once so that no air enters the chest
option_2: Check the drain and the bottle for a kink or a leak and call the doctor
option_3: Ask the man to take slow deep breaths and record the reading in the chart
option_4: Record the reading in the chart and give oxygen
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check the drain and the bottle for a kink or a leak and call the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A sudden shortness of breath with a low saturation in a man with a chest drain calls for the drain and the bottle to be checked for a kink or a leak, and the doctor to be called at once.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man with a chest drain who becomes short of breath with an oxygen saturation of 88 per cent

Priority Principle: ABC / Chest drain

Why Not Others: (a) Clamping the drain can trap air inside the chest and is not done at once; (c) Slow breaths and a note leave the fault of the drain in place; (d) A note and oxygen leave the fault of the drain untouched.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a clamp seems the sure way to stop air entering the chest.

5-Second Recall: Chest tube wale me achanak saans phoolna = tube-bottle check karo, doctor ko bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The whole length of the drain is inspected before the chest air is blamed.

question: A nurse on the ward must prepare a bleach solution to disinfect a rubber tube that is used again for a client. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wash the tube with soap and water and keep it in a clean box
option_2: Soak the tube in a strong bleach powder for a short time
option_3: Work out the strength needed and soak the tube in the solution for the set time
option_4: Boil the tube in water for a minute and keep it in saline
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Work out the strength needed and soak the tube in the solution for the set time

Clinical Rationale: The strength of the bleach solution is worked out and the tube is soaked for the set time, because a strong solution harms the rubber and a weak one does NOT kill the germs.

Key Clue: rubber tube that is reused and must be disinfected with bleach solution

Priority Principle: Infection control / Disinfection

Why Not Others: (a) Washing with soap cleans the tube but does not disinfect it; (b) A strong bleach solution harms the rubber of the tube and the nurse's hands; (d) Boiling for one minute does not kill every germ on the tube.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because soap and water seem the whole cleaning of a tube.

5-Second Recall: Bleach ki taakat naapo, aur tube ko poora samay usme doobao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A disinfectant works only at the right strength and for the right time.

question: A nurse must give the morning drugs to a 45-year-old man on the ward through his nasogastric tube. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the drugs by mouth as usual and continue the feed
option_2: Mix all the morning drugs in a cup and pour the mixture down the tube
option_3: Put the tablets down the tube whole with a small amount of water
option_4: Check the order and the form of each drug and give them one by one with a water flush
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check the order and the form of each drug and give them one by one with a water flush

Clinical Rationale: The order and the form of each drug are checked and the drugs are given one by one with a water flush between them, so that the tube does NOT block.

Key Clue: morning drugs to be given through the nasogastric tube of a 45-year-old man

Priority Principle: Procedure / Drugs by tube

Why Not Others: (a) Drugs by mouth in a man with a nasogastric tube are not safe; (b) A mixture of several drugs may set like a lump and block the tube; (c) A whole tablet sticks in the tube and is not absorbed.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because one mixture seems the quick way on a busy round.

5-Second Recall: Tube se dawa ek-ek do, beech me paani se wash karo - mila kar nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: Each drug goes down the tube alone and with a water flush.

question: A 50-year-old woman on the ward with a colostomy bag says that stool is leaking under the ring of the bag and that her skin is burning. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put another ring over the old ring and press the bag down hard
option_2: Remove the bag, clean the skin with warm water and fit a bag of the right size
option_3: Wash the skin with spirit and leave it open to the air
option_4: Note the leak in the chart and ask for a fresh bag in the morning
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Remove the bag, clean the skin with warm water and fit a bag of the right size

Clinical Rationale: A leak under the ring of the bag burns the skin, so the bag is removed, the skin is cleaned with warm water and a bag of the right size is fitted at once.

Key Clue: 50-year-old woman with a colostomy bag, a leak under the ring and burning skin

Priority Principle: Skin safety / Colostomy bag

Why Not Others: (a) A second ring over the old one holds stool against the skin; (c) Spirit on the skin around the opening dries and harms it; (d) Waiting until the morning allows a sore to form on the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because another ring seems the fast stop of the leak.

5-Second Recall: Bag ke neeche leak = bag hatao, chamdi saaf karo, sahi naap ka bag lagao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The opening of the bag is matched to the size of the stoma.

question: A nurse on the ward has four clients, and one 60-year-old man with a tracheostomy has noisy breathing with a rising pulse. Which client should the nurse see FIRST?
option_1: The man with the tracheostomy who breathes noisily
option_2: The client who asks for a warm drink of milk
option_3: The client who wants the pillow to be changed
option_4: The client whose family asks when the doctor will come
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The man with the tracheostomy who breathes noisily

Clinical Rationale: A man with a tracheostomy who breathes noisily and has a rising pulse is short of air, so he is seen before every other client on the ward.

Key Clue: four clients and one 60-year-old man with a tracheostomy whose breathing is noisy

Priority Principle: ABC / Airway

Why Not Others: (b) The warm milk can wait for the drink round; (c) The pillow is a small matter of the room; (d) When the doctor will come is a desk matter.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the milk seems the need the nurse can meet fastest.

5-Second Recall: Tracheostomy wale ki saans ki awaaz = pehle usi ko dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A noise in the breathing of a tracheostomy client means an airway that is not clear.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse on the ward notices that the drain tube of a 55-year-old man has come out partly, while the stitch still holds it to the skin. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the length of the tube and do the morning dressing
option_2: Push the tube back to its previous mark with clean hands
option_3: Pull the tube out completely and press the site with a pad
option_4: Cover the site with a sterile dressing and inform the doctor at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Cover the site with a sterile dressing and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A drain that has come out partly is covered with a sterile dressing and the doctor is informed at once, because pushing it back carries germs into the wound.

Key Clue: drain tube of a 55-year-old man that has come out partly while the stitch still holds it

Priority Principle: Safety / Drain

Why Not Others: (a) A note and the usual dressing leave the wound open to the air; (b) Pushing the tube back takes the germs of the skin into the wound; (c) Pulling a tube that is still stitched can tear the wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because putting the tube back seems the tidy step.

5-Second Recall: Drain bahar aaya = wapas dhakka mat do, sterile dressing aur doctor abhi.

PNC Exam Pearl: A drain is never pushed back by the nurse.

question: A nurse must give oxygen by mask to a 65-year-old man on the ward who has a moist mouth and a cough with sputum. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the man to keep the mask off until the cough has gone
option_2: Put the mask on the face and turn the flow to the highest mark
option_3: Check the order and the water in the humidifier and choose a mask of the right size
option_4: Note the cough in the chart and give the oxygen by nasal prongs
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Check the order and the water in the humidifier and choose a mask of the right size

Clinical Rationale: The order and the water in the humidifier are checked and a mask of the right size is chosen before the oxygen is given, so that the air the man breathes is moist and the mask fits.

Key Clue: oxygen by mask for a 65-year-old man with a moist mouth and a cough with sputum

Priority Principle: Procedure / Oxygen by mask

Why Not Others: (a) A mask kept off leaves the man without the air he needs; (b) A high flow without an order and a mask of the wrong size harm the man; (d) A change to the prongs is a fresh step and not the first one.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the highest mark of the flow seems the fastest help.

5-Second Recall: Mask se oxygen se pehle order, humidifier ka paani aur mask ka naap dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The water in the bottle is checked so that the oxygen is moist.

question: A nurse with two helpers must move a 60-year-old woman on the ward who cannot help herself from the bed to the trolley. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the woman to hold the nurse's neck and step on to the trolley
option_2: Take the woman under the arms and ask the helpers to lift her legs
option_3: Pull the woman on to a sheet towards the trolley from the side
option_4: Raise the bed to the height of the trolley, lock the wheels and put the rail down
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Raise the bed to the height of the trolley, lock the wheels and put the rail down

Clinical Rationale: The bed is raised to the height of the trolley, the wheels are locked and the rail is put down before the woman is moved, so that the move is safe for the woman and the staff.

Key Clue: 60-year-old woman who cannot help herself and needs to be moved from the bed to the trolley with two helpers

Priority Principle: Procedure / Safe move

Why Not Others: (a) Holding the nurse's neck is not safe for either of them; (b) A lift under the arms bends the woman and strains the staff; (c) A pull without a plan harms the staff's back and the woman's skin.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a quick lift seems the way to save time.

5-Second Recall: Move se pehle bed ki unchaai trolley ke barabar, wheels lock, rail neeche.

PNC Exam Pearl: The move is planned by the height and the wheels before any hands touch the client.

question: A nurse on the ward notices that the mark on the nasogastric tube of a 55-year-old woman is now two centimetres farther out than the recorded mark. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the feed down the tube as ordered and note the mark in the chart
option_2: Push the tube in by two centimetres to the mark on the chart
option_3: Hold the feed and the drugs given by the tube and check the mark with the order and the doctor
option_4: Remove the tube and ask the nurse to pass a fresh tube at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Hold the feed and the drugs given by the tube and check the mark with the order and the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A tube that has come out by two centimetres may no longer lie in the stomach, so the feed and the drugs are held and the mark is checked with the order and the doctor.

Key Clue: mark on the nasogastric tube of a 55-year-old woman that is two centimetres farther out than the chart

Priority Principle: Safety / Nasogastric tube

Why Not Others: (a) A feed down a tube that has moved can enter the lungs; (b) Pushing the tube in may place it in the airway; (d) A fresh tube is passed only on the doctor's order.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the mark on the chart seems the place where the tube must sit.

5-Second Recall: Tube ka nishaan badal gaya = feed roko, doctor se check karwao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The mark of the tube is read before every feed.

question: A 2-year-old child on the ward has a scalp drip, and the mother says that the child pulls at the line with the hand. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tie both the child's hands to the sides of the bed
option_2: Secure the line with a splint and tape and teach the mother how to hold the child
option_3: Remove the drip and give the fluid by mouth instead
option_4: Ask the mother to sit farther away from the child's bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Secure the line with a splint and tape and teach the mother how to hold the child

Clinical Rationale: A line that the child pulls at is secured with a splint and tape and the mother is taught how to hold the child, so that the vein is NOT harmed.

Key Clue: 2-year-old child with a scalp drip who pulls at the line with the hand

Priority Principle: Safety / Drip line

Why Not Others: (a) Tying a child's hands is a last resort and needs an order; (c) A drip is removed only on the doctor's order; (d) The mother away from the bed leaves the child alone with the line.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a tie seems the sure way to save the line.

5-Second Recall: Bachcha line kheench raha = splint lagao, maa ko sambhalna sikhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The line is secured before any talk of restraint.

question: A 45-year-old man on the ward says that the dressing on his arm feels tight, and the fingers below the dressing look pale and feel numb. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Open the dressing and look at the wound and the colour of the fingers
option_2: Give a tablet for the pain and ask the man to move his fingers
option_3: Raise the arm on a pillow and note the colour after an hour
option_4: Put a fresh dressing over the old one with a looser band
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Open the dressing and look at the wound and the colour of the fingers

Clinical Rationale: A tight dressing with pale and numb fingers is opened and the wound and fingers are examined, because the blood flow below the dressing is in danger.

Key Clue: 45-year-old man with a tight dressing on the arm and pale, numb fingers below it

Priority Principle: Circulation / Dressing

Why Not Others: (b) A tablet for the pain and moving the fingers do not restore the blood flow; (c) An hour of watching allows the fingers to become cold and blue; (d) A fresh dressing over the old one keeps the tightness inside.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because raising the arm seems the safe FIRST care.

5-Second Recall: Dressing kas rahi aur ungliyan safed = dressing kholo, khoon ka flow dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A dressing that is tight is opened before any drug for the pain is given.

question: A 50-year-old woman on the ward uses an insulin pen twice a day, and the nurse finds that the pen was left in the ward freezer last night. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Keep the pen aside and take a fresh pen for the morning dose
option_2: Warm the frozen pen in the hands and give the dose from it
option_3: Shake the frozen pen well and give the morning dose
option_4: Note the frozen pen in the chart and give the dose in the evening
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the pen aside and take a fresh pen for the morning dose

Clinical Rationale: Insulin that has been frozen has lost its potency, so the pen is kept aside and a fresh pen is taken for the morning dose.

Key Clue: insulin pen of a 50-year-old woman that was left in the ward freezer last night

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Insulin

Why Not Others: (b) A frozen pen has lost its potency and the dose from it is wrong; (c) Shaking the pen does not restore the potency of frozen insulin; (d) A dose given in the evening leaves the woman without her morning dose.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because warming in the hands seems the way to save the drug.

5-Second Recall: Freezer me rakhi insulin phenko - nayi pen se dose do.

PNC Exam Pearl: Insulin that has been frozen or heated is never used.

question: A nurse on the ward must measure the blood pressure of a 50-year-old man with a thick arm, and the only cuff on the trolley is small for the arm. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the reading on the man's thigh with the same small cuff
option_2: Take the reading with the small cuff and record the number in the chart
option_3: Press the small cuff tighter on the arm for a true reading
option_4: Take a cuff of the right size for the arm before the reading is taken
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Take a cuff of the right size for the arm before the reading is taken

Clinical Rationale: A cuff that is small for the arm gives a reading that is too high, so a cuff of the right size is taken before the blood pressure is measured.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man with a thick arm and only a small cuff on the trolley for the blood pressure

Priority Principle: Procedure / Blood pressure

Why Not Others: (a) A reading on the thigh is a different measure and not the pressure of the arm; (b) A small cuff on a thick arm gives a falsely high reading; (c) A tighter cuff makes the reading even higher and harms the arm.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the number of the cuff seems the whole of the reading.

5-Second Recall: Moti baazu ke liye bada cuff - chhota cuff galat reading deta hai.

PNC Exam Pearl: The width of the cuff is matched to the arm before the pressure is read.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse on the ward must apply the fetal heart monitor belt to the abdomen of a 25-year-old woman in labour, and the woman has a full bladder and the belt keeps slipping. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Remove the belt and listen with the stethoscope once an hour
option_2: Press the belt tighter on the abdomen so that it does NOT slip again
option_3: Ask the woman to pass urine and apply the belt again over the fetal back
option_4: Ask the woman to lie flat on her back with the legs raised
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Ask the woman to pass urine and apply the belt again over the fetal back

Clinical Rationale: A full bladder and a slipping belt give a poor tracing, so the woman is asked to pass urine and the belt is applied again over the fetal back.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman in labour with a full bladder and a slipping fetal heart monitor belt

Priority Principle: Safety / Fetal heart monitor

Why Not Others: (a) Listening once an hour leaves the labour without a watch on the heart; (b) A tighter belt presses the uterus and gives a poor tracing; (d) A flat position with the legs raised presses the great vessel of the mother.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tight belt seems the sure hold of the monitor.

5-Second Recall: Full bladder aur belt fisalti hai = peshaab karao, belt phir lagao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The fetal heart tracing is read best over the back of the baby.

question: A 65-year-old woman on the ward has an ice pack on the knee, and the nurse notes that the skin under the pack is pale and hard to touch. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put a fresh ice pack over the old one with a cloth between
option_2: Remove the ice pack and look at the skin of the knee
option_3: Press the ice pack down hard so that the cold goes deep
option_4: Note the colour of the skin in the chart and leave the pack for an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Remove the ice pack and look at the skin of the knee

Clinical Rationale: Pale and hard skin under an ice pack shows harm to the skin from the cold, so the pack is removed at once and the skin is examined.

Key Clue: 65-year-old woman with an ice pack on the knee and skin under it that is pale and hard to touch

Priority Principle: Safety / Ice pack

Why Not Others: (a) A fresh pack over a pale knee harms the skin even more; (c) A hard press of the pack presses the cold into the skin; (d) An hour more of the ice brings a sore of the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because fresh ice seems the way to bring the swelling down.

5-Second Recall: Ice ke neeche safed-sakht chamdi = ice hatao, chamdi dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: An ice pack is applied over a cloth and inspected every few minutes.

question: A nurse checks the screen of a pump running a drug into the vein of a 50-year-old man on the ward and reads 30 millilitres per hour, while the doctor's order is for 10 millilitres per hour. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Let the pump run and note the screen reading in the chart
option_2: Stop the pump and set the rate again to the doctor's order
option_3: Change the screen of the pump and continue at the same rate
option_4: Ask the man to press the bell when the pump makes a sound
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the pump and set the rate again to the doctor's order

Clinical Rationale: A pump that runs at three times the ordered rate is stopped and reset at once, because a drug that enters quickly can harm the man.

Key Clue: pump running a drug into the vein of a 50-year-old man at 30 millilitres per hour with an order for 10

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Pump rate

Why Not Others: (a) A note of the reading leaves the strong rate running into the vein; (c) A fresh screen at the same rate gives the same wrong dose; (d) A bell in the man's hands is no guard against a rate that is wrong.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the screen seems the fault that must be changed.

5-Second Recall: Pump 30 mL/hr par aur order 10 = pump roko, rate dobara set karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The screen of a pump is read against the order at every round.

question: A nurse must use the suction machine for the airway of a 60-year-old man on the ward who has a tracheostomy tube. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Check that the machine works and set the suction pressure
option_2: Pass the suction catheter into the man's airway
option_3: Ask the man to take a deep breath and to cough
option_4: Wash the hands and put on gloves for the step
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check that the machine works and set the suction pressure

Clinical Rationale: The suction machine is checked and the pressure is set before the suction catheter is passed, because a suction that does NOT work in the hour of need costs the airway.

Key Clue: suction machine to be used on a 60-year-old man with a tracheostomy tube

Priority Principle: Safety / Suction machine

Why Not Others: (b) A catheter passed before the machine is checked may sit in an airway with no pull; (c) A deep breath is asked for after the machine and the pressure are ready; (d) Gloves are put on after the machine is set right.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the state of the man seems the hour of the step.

5-Second Recall: Suction machine se pehle: machine chalti hai ya nahi aur pressure set karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The machine is checked at the bedside before the airway needs it.

question: A nurse on the ward finds that the packet of sterile gloves kept for a client has been open since the morning and the outside of the box is soiled. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wipe the outside of the box and keep the packet for the round
option_2: Use the gloves of the open packet because the hands will be clean inside
option_3: Turn the packet inside out and use the gloves at the bottom
option_4: Throw the gloves of the open packet away and take a fresh sterile packet
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Throw the gloves of the open packet away and take a fresh sterile packet

Clinical Rationale: A packet of sterile gloves that has stood open with a soiled box is no longer sterile, so it is thrown away and a fresh packet is taken at once.

Key Clue: packet of sterile gloves on the trolley that has been open since the morning with a soiled box

Priority Principle: Infection control / Sterile gloves

Why Not Others: (a) A wiped box does not make the gloves of an open packet sterile; (b) A clean hand inside a soiled packet gives a glove that is not sterile; (c) A packet turned inside out still holds the germs of the air.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a pair of gloves seems a pair of gloves whatever the packet.

5-Second Recall: Khula hua sterile packet = phenko, naya packet kholo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A packet that is open is no longer counted as sterile.

question: A nurse must set a drip of 500 millilitres of fluid for a client on the ward to run over eight hours with a set that gives 15 drops per millilitre. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Set the flow by eye and note the time on the bottle
option_2: Open the clamp wide so that the fluid runs fast at the start
option_3: Work out the drops per minute and set the flow to that number
option_4: Ask the man to press the bell when the bottle is empty
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Work out the drops per minute and set the flow to that number

Clinical Rationale: Five hundred millilitres over eight hours with 15 drops per millilitre gives about 16 drops per minute, and the flow is set to that number before the drip runs.

Key Clue: drip of 500 millilitres over eight hours with a set that gives 15 drops per millilitre

Priority Principle: Procedure / Drip rate

Why Not Others: (a) A flow set by eye has no number and no check; (b) A wide clamp at the start gives the fluid faster than the order; (d) A bell in the man's hands is no guard against a wrong rate.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the eye of the nurse seems the measure of a drip.

5-Second Recall: 500 mL / 8 ghante, 15 drops/mL = lagbhag 16 drops per minute.

PNC Exam Pearl: The drops per minute are worked out before the clamp is set.

question: A 40-year-old man on the ward asks the nurse to look at the chart and the reports of his own tests. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Refuse the reports and ask him to speak to the doctor alone
option_2: Show the man the reports of his tests and explain the findings with care
option_3: Note the request in the chart and call the family for a talk
option_4: Take a copy of the reports and send it to the family
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Show the man the reports of his tests and explain the findings with care

Clinical Rationale: A client has a right to know the reports of his own tests, so they are shown and explained with care to him.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man who asks the nurse to see the chart and the reports of his own tests

Priority Principle: Ethics / Right to know

Why Not Others: (a) A refusal takes away a right that the client holds; (c) A call to the family does not give the man the reports he asked for; (d) The reports are sent to the family on the wish of the client.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the doctor seems the one person who may speak of tests.

5-Second Recall: Client ko apni report dekhne ka haq hai - samjha kar dikhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The findings are told to the client with care and in words that he understands.

question: A nurse must take the temperature of a 2-month-old baby on the ward, and the only thermometer on the trolley is marked for the mouth. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the temperature under the arm of the baby with a fresh thermometer
option_2: Put the mouth thermometer under the baby's tongue
option_3: Put the thermometer into the baby's back passage at once
option_4: Judge the heat by laying a hand on the baby's skin
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Take the temperature under the arm of the baby with a fresh thermometer

Clinical Rationale: The temperature of a 2-month-old baby is taken under the arm with a fresh thermometer, because the axilla is safe and the mouth of a baby cannot hold a thermometer.

Key Clue: 2-month-old baby on the ward with only a thermometer that is marked for the mouth

Priority Principle: Procedure / Temperature of a baby

Why Not Others: (b) A 2-month-old baby cannot keep a thermometer safe under the tongue; (c) The back passage is a step of last choice and needs care and a fresh thermometer; (d) A hand on the skin tells that the baby is warm and not how warm.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the back passage seems the true place of a temperature.

5-Second Recall: Chhote bachche ka tapman bagal me lo, muh ka thermometer nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The place for the temperature is chosen with the age of the child.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse at a sub-centre finds the paper of a syringe packet torn, and the syringe kept for a client who comes to the OPD lies against the cloth of the trolley. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the torn packet in the register and continue the session
option_2: Use the syringe of the torn packet after a wash with spirit
option_3: Keep the syringe in the packet and use it for the next client
option_4: Throw the syringe of the torn packet away and take a fresh packet
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Throw the syringe of the torn packet away and take a fresh packet

Clinical Rationale: A syringe from a torn packet is no longer sterile, so it is thrown away and a fresh packet is taken before any injection is given.

Key Clue: syringe from a torn packet that lies against the cloth of the trolley at a sub-centre

Priority Principle: Infection control / Sterile syringe

Why Not Others: (a) A note in the register leaves the fault for the next client; (b) A wash of the outside does not make the inside of the syringe sterile; (c) An injection with this syringe puts germs into the body of the client.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a wash with spirit seems the way to clean a syringe.

5-Second Recall: Syringe ka packet phata = phenko, naya packet kholo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A packet that is torn has lost the sterile state of the syringe.

question: A 45-year-old man who takes lithium has a serum level of 0.4 mEq/L, and the family says that he has become very cheerful with less sleep. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the family that a cheerful state is a good sign of the treatment
option_2: Give the next dose of the drug as ordered and note the change of state
option_3: Note the low level with the change of state and inform the doctor at once
option_4: Wait for the next level report and watch the man's sleep
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Note the low level with the change of state and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A level of 0.4 mEq/L with a cheerful state and less sleep points to a dose that is too low, so the level and the change are noted and the doctor is informed at once.

Key Clue: 45-year-old man on lithium with a level of 0.4 mEq/L, a cheerful state and less sleep

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Drug level

Why Not Others: (a) A cheerful state with less sleep is a sign of illness and not of healing; (b) The same dose at a low level keeps the man's state rising; (d) A wait for the next report lets the man's state rise further.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a cheerful man seems a man who is getting well.

5-Second Recall: Level kam aur neend kam, khush bahut = dose ki jaanch, doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The level of the drug is read with the state of the client and not alone.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A 25-year-old woman on the ward after childbirth has a urine bag hanging on the side rail above the level of the bladder, and the tube is looped on the bed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Empty the bag into a pot and hang it back on the rail
option_2: Raise the bag higher so that the urine runs out of the bladder fast
option_3: Put the bag below the level of the bladder and free the loop of the tube
option_4: Note the state of the bag in the chart and leave it for the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Put the bag below the level of the bladder and free the loop of the tube

Clinical Rationale: A bag above the bladder with a looped tube lets urine run back into the bladder, so the bag is put below the level of the bladder and the tube is freed at once.

Key Clue: urine bag of a 25-year-old woman after childbirth that hangs above the level of the bladder with a looped tube

Priority Principle: Safety / Urine bag

Why Not Others: (a) Hanging the bag on the same rail leaves the level wrong; (b) A higher bag makes the urine run back into the bladder; (d) A note at the round leaves the urine running back for hours.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a higher bag seems the faster flow of the urine.

5-Second Recall: Urine bag bladder se neeche - tube me loop nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The bag is kept below the bladder at every hour of the day.

question: A nurse at a sub-centre has just given an injection to a 30-year-old man who attends the clinic. Which action should the nurse take FIRST with the needle?
option_1: Put the needle in the paper waste bin of the centre
option_2: Put the cover back on the needle and keep it for the next injection
option_3: Keep the needle on the tray and clean it with spirit
option_4: Put the needle in the sharps box at once without putting the cover back
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Put the needle in the sharps box at once without putting the cover back

Clinical Rationale: The needle goes into the sharps box at once and the cover is NOT put back, because a needle that is capped again is the common cause of a needle-stick injury.

Key Clue: needle that has just been used for an injection at a sub-centre

Priority Principle: Safety / Needle and sharps

Why Not Others: (a) A needle in the paper bin comes back through the hands of the cleaner; (b) A needle capped again is the common cause of a needle-stick injury; (c) A needle kept on the tray is a danger to every person at the centre.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the cover seems the safe home of a needle.

5-Second Recall: Sui ka cover wapas mat lagao - seedha sharps box me daalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A needle is never put back into its cover by the hand.

question: A nurse must give a drug by an inhaler with a spacer to a 5-year-old child on the ward who has a tight chest. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Shake the inhaler, fit it on the spacer and teach the child to breathe in slowly
option_2: Put the mouth of the inhaler straight into the child's mouth
option_3: Ask the child to breathe out hard into the spacer before the puff
option_4: Give two puffs of the drug at once so that the chest opens fast
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Shake the inhaler, fit it on the spacer and teach the child to breathe in slowly

Clinical Rationale: The inhaler is shaken and fitted on the spacer and the child is taught to breathe in slowly, so that the drug reaches the small airways and NOT the mouth.

Key Clue: drug by an inhaler with a spacer for a 5-year-old child with a tight chest

Priority Principle: Procedure / Inhaler and spacer

Why Not Others: (b) An inhaler straight in the mouth leaves much of the drug on the tongue; (c) A hard breath into the spacer blows the drug out of it; (d) Two puffs at once are not ordered and do not reach the airways better.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a breath into the spacer seems the right use of it.

5-Second Recall: Inhaler hilao, spacer lagao, dheere saans andar - yahi tarika.

PNC Exam Pearl: A spacer is used so that the drug reaches the airways of a small child.

question: A nurse on the ward has four clients, and one 70-year-old man with chronic lung disease is confused with an oxygen saturation of 85 per cent. Which client should the nurse see FIRST?
option_1: The client who asks for help to walk to the bath
option_2: The 70-year-old man who is confused with an oxygen saturation of 85 per cent
option_3: The client who wants the window to be shut
option_4: The client whose family asks when the visiting hour is
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The 70-year-old man who is confused with an oxygen saturation of 85 per cent

Clinical Rationale: A man who is confused with a low oxygen saturation is short of air in the brain, so he is seen before every other client on the ward.

Key Clue: four clients and one 70-year-old man with chronic lung disease who is confused with an oxygen saturation of 85 per cent

Priority Principle: ABC / Air and oxygen

Why Not Others: (a) A walk to the bath can wait for a short time; (c) The window is a small matter of the room; (d) The visiting hour is a desk matter.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the walk seems the need the nurse can meet fastest.

5-Second Recall: Oxygen 85 aur confusion = pehle usi ko dekho, oxygen do.

PNC Exam Pearl: A new confusion in lung disease is read as a fall of the oxygen.

question: A nurse must give a drug into the vein of a 60-year-old man on the ward, and the site of the cannula in his arm is red and hot with a slight swelling. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Remove the cannula, press the site and take a fresh line in the other arm
option_2: Wash the line with saline and use it for the drug
option_3: Push the drug into the line and note the redness in the chart
option_4: Put a warm pack on the red site and continue the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Remove the cannula, press the site and take a fresh line in the other arm

Clinical Rationale: A red and hot site with a swelling is an infection of the vein, so the cannula is removed, the site is pressed and a fresh line is taken in the other arm.

Key Clue: cannula site in the arm of a 60-year-old man that is red and hot with a slight swelling

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Intravenous line

Why Not Others: (b) Washing the line pushes the germs up into the blood; (c) A drug pushed into a line of this kind makes the infection worse; (d) A warm pack on the red site hides the infection of the vein.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a push through the line seems the duty of the round.

5-Second Recall: Cannula ki jagah laal-garam = line nikaalo, doosre haath me nayi line.

PNC Exam Pearl: A line with a red and hot site is removed and never used again.

question: A nurse must give a bed bath to a 60-year-old man on the ward who has a nasogastric tube for feeding. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Remove the tube and put it back after the man's bath
option_2: Take the tape off the tube and wash the face well near it
option_3: Lower the head of the bed flat so that the tube does NOT pull
option_4: See that the tube is taped well and lay the man with the head of the bed raised
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) See that the tube is taped well and lay the man with the head of the bed raised

Clinical Rationale: The tube is checked to be taped well and the man is laid with the head of the bed raised, so that the tube does NOT pull and the feed does NOT come back up.

Key Clue: bed bath for a 60-year-old man with a nasogastric tube for feeding

Priority Principle: Procedure / Bath and a tube

Why Not Others: (a) A tube is never removed and put back for a bath; (b) Removing the tape lets the tube move during the bath; (c) A flat head of the bed lets the feed come back up the tube.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a flat man seems the easy man for a bath.

5-Second Recall: Nose tube wale ko nehlane se pehle tube ki tape aur bed ka sir dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The tube is secured before the body is washed.

question: A nurse on the ward sees a 70-year-old woman who walks with a frame stand up from the chair without the frame and sway. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Bring the frame to her and ask her to take a step to it
option_2: Call from the desk and ask her to sit down again
option_3: Move to her side at once and hold her arm to keep her from a fall
option_4: Note the state in the chart and teach her NOT to stand without the frame
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Move to her side at once and hold her arm to keep her from a fall

Clinical Rationale: A woman who stands without her frame and sways is about to fall, so the nurse moves to her side at once and holds her arm.

Key Clue: 70-year-old woman who walks with a frame, stands without it and sways on her feet

Priority Principle: Safety / Fall

Why Not Others: (a) A step to the frame is not safe while she sways; (b) A call from the desk is too far and too late for a woman who sways; (d) A note and a teaching after the fall are too late.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the frame seems the thing that keeps her from a fall.

5-Second Recall: Frame chhod kar khadi aur jhool rahi hai = turant paas jao aur sahaara do.

PNC Exam Pearl: The hands of the nurse are the first guard of a client who is about to fall.

question: A nurse in the newborn unit looks at a 1-day-old baby lying under the warmer, and the baby's temperature reads 36 degrees Celsius with cold hands and feet. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the baby out of the warmer and hold him near the mother
option_2: Cover the baby's head and set the warmer to the right heat
option_3: Put a thick blanket over the baby and go to the next cot
option_4: Note the temperature in the chart and take it again after an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Cover the baby's head and set the warmer to the right heat

Clinical Rationale: A 1-day-old baby with a temperature of 36 degrees Celsius and cold hands is losing heat, so the head is covered and the warmer is set to the right heat at once.

Key Clue: 1-day-old baby under the warmer with a temperature of 36 degrees Celsius and cold hands and feet

Priority Principle: Newborn / Baby heat

Why Not Others: (a) A baby taken out of the warmer loses more heat in the room; (c) A thick blanket over the baby does not set the warmer right; (d) An hour of waiting lets the baby lose more heat.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a blanket seems the warm answer for a cold baby.

5-Second Recall: Naya bachcha thanda = sir dhako, warmer sahi set karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The head of a newborn is covered because much heat is lost from it.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse on the ward looks at the tape that seals a pack from the autoclave before the dressing of a client and sees that the marks on the tape have NOT changed colour. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Use the pack because the tape looks dry and whole
option_2: Keep the pack aside as NOT sterile and run the load of the machine again
option_3: Put the pack in the machine for a short time of five minutes
option_4: Note the tape in the machine book and use the pack later
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Keep the pack aside as NOT sterile and run the load of the machine again

Clinical Rationale: A tape whose marks have NOT changed shows that the load has NOT been through the right heat, so the pack is kept aside and the load is run again.

Key Clue: tape that seals a pack from the autoclave with marks that have NOT changed colour

Priority Principle: Infection control / Autoclave

Why Not Others: (a) A dry and whole tape does not tell that the load was sterile; (c) A short time of five minutes does not sterilise the load; (d) Use of the pack later puts a pack that is not sterile on a wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a whole tape seems a sterile pack.

5-Second Recall: Tape ka rang nahi badla = pack sterile nahi, load dobara chalao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The mark of the tape tells the truth about the load of the machine.

question: A nurse must give a bed pan to a 70-year-old woman on the ward who cannot get up from the bed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Place the pan flat on the bed and ask the woman to roll on to it
option_2: Ask the woman to lift herself up and slide the pan under
option_3: Warm the pan, raise the head of the bed and place the pan under her
option_4: Give the woman a drink of water and wait for the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Warm the pan, raise the head of the bed and place the pan under her

Clinical Rationale: The pan is warmed and the head of the bed is raised before the pan is placed, so that the woman is comfortable and the skin of her back is safe.

Key Clue: bed pan for a 70-year-old woman who cannot get up from the bed

Priority Principle: Procedure / Bed pan

Why Not Others: (a) A pan is placed on the bed after the head of the bed is raised; (b) A woman who cannot get up is not asked to lift herself on the bed; (d) A drink and a wait leave the woman with a full bladder.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because lifting the woman seems the way to place a pan.

5-Second Recall: Bed pan pehle garam karo, bed ka sir uncha karo, phir rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The pan is warmed because a cold pan makes the woman hold her urine.

question: A nurse who answers the bell of an 80-year-old woman finds her on the floor beside the bed, and the floor near the bath is wet. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Call the family and ask what she was doing on the floor
option_2: Lift her up at once and put her back into the bed
option_3: Ask her to stand and walk with help to the bed
option_4: Stay with her, keep her still and check the airway and the pulse
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Stay with her, keep her still and check the airway and the pulse

Clinical Rationale: A woman found on the floor is kept still while the airway and the pulse are checked, because a lift before the check can harm a broken bone or the spine.

Key Clue: 80-year-old woman found on the floor beside the bed with a wet floor near the bath

Priority Principle: Safety / Fall

Why Not Others: (a) A talk with the family comes after the state of the woman is known; (b) A lift at once can harm a bone or the spine that is already injured; (c) A stand and a walk after a fall can bring a second fall.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a quick lift seems the kind care of an old woman.

5-Second Recall: Farsh par mili budhiya = hilaao mat, saans-nadi check karo, madad bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A client found on the floor is checked where she lies before she is moved.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse must give a pump feed to a 50-year-old man on the ward, and the order reads 500 millilitres over four hours. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Work out the rate of the feed and check the position of the tube
option_2: Set the pump to run the feed as fast as the machine allows
option_3: Give the feed in one hour so that the man can rest after it
option_4: Give the feed by mouth in small sips instead of by the pump
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Work out the rate of the feed and check the position of the tube

Clinical Rationale: Five hundred millilitres over four hours gives about 125 millilitres per hour, and the rate and the position of the tube are checked before the feed runs.

Key Clue: pump feed of 500 millilitres over four hours for a 50-year-old man

Priority Principle: Procedure / Pump feed

Why Not Others: (b) A feed as fast as the machine allows brings vomiting and loose stools; (c) A feed in one hour is four times the ordered rate; (d) A man who needs a tube feed cannot take the feed by mouth.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a feed in one hour seems the rest that a sick man needs.

5-Second Recall: 500 mL / 4 ghante = 125 mL per hour, tube ki jagah check karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A pump feed is given at the ordered rate and watched for the belly.

question: A nurse must empty the urine bag of a 70-year-old man on the ward who has a urinary catheter. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wash the hands, put on gloves and keep the outlet of the bag from touching the pot
option_2: Hold the bag above the level of the bladder and open the outlet
option_3: Empty the bag into the bed pan and keep the outlet open
option_4: Remove the catheter and ask the man to pass urine in the pot
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Wash the hands, put on gloves and keep the outlet of the bag from touching the pot

Clinical Rationale: The hands are washed and gloves are put on and the outlet is kept from touching the pot, so that germs do NOT go back up the tube into the bladder.

Key Clue: urine bag of a 70-year-old man with a urinary catheter and a pot to empty it into

Priority Principle: Procedure / Urine bag

Why Not Others: (b) A bag held above the bladder lets the urine run back inside; (c) An outlet that touches the pot takes the germs up the tube; (d) A catheter is removed only on the doctor's order.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the pot seems the whole work of emptying a bag.

5-Second Recall: Bag khaali karte waqt outlet pot ko na chhue, aur bag neeche rahe.

PNC Exam Pearl: The outlet of the bag is kept clean and off every surface.

question: A nurse must clean the wound of a 50-year-old man on the ward that has a drain on the far side and a soiled part near the near edge. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean from the soiled part towards the clean part
option_2: Clean from the clean part of the wound towards the soiled part
option_3: Clean the drain and the wound with the same swab
option_4: Wash the wound with the water of the ward and dry it
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clean from the clean part of the wound towards the soiled part

Clinical Rationale: The wound is cleaned from the clean part towards the soiled part, so that the germs of the soiled part are NOT carried into the clean flesh.

Key Clue: wound of a 50-year-old man with a drain on the far side and a soiled part near the near edge

Priority Principle: Infection control / Wound

Why Not Others: (a) Cleaning from the soiled part carries the germs into the clean flesh; (c) One swab for the drain and the wound carries the germs across the wound; (d) The water of the ward is not clean for a wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the soiled part seems the part that must be cleaned FIRST.

5-Second Recall: Ghaav saaf hisse se gande hisse ki taraf saaf karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fresh swab for each part keeps the wound from the germs of its own edge.

question: A 55-year-old man on the ward who is fed through a nasogastric tube now has a distended abdomen with no bowel sounds on auscultation. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put a warm pack on the abdomen and continue the feed as ordered
option_2: Give the rest of the feed slowly and watch the man's abdomen
option_3: Stop the feed, keep the man sitting up and inform the doctor at once
option_4: Note the abdominal distension in the chart and give the feed later
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stop the feed, keep the man sitting up and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A distended abdomen with no bowel sounds in a man on a tube feed points to the feed NOT moving, so the feed is stopped, the man is kept sitting up and the doctor is informed at once.

Key Clue: 55-year-old man fed through a nasogastric tube with a distended abdomen and no bowel sounds

Priority Principle: Safety / Tube feed

Why Not Others: (a) A warm pack does not set right a belly that is not moving; (b) The rest of the feed enters a belly that has stopped moving; (d) A later feed makes the distension worse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the rest of the feed seems the full care of the man.

5-Second Recall: Tube feed ke baad pet phoola aur awaaz nahi = feed band karo, doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A belly without sound in a tube feed is watched before the next feed.

question: A 45-year-old woman on the ward calls the nurse and says that the dressing of the wound has come off in the bed and the wound is open. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the state of the dressing in the chart and renew it at the round
option_2: Ask the woman to hold the wound with the hand of the bed sheet
option_3: Wash the wound with the water of the ward and leave it open
option_4: Cover the wound with a sterile dressing at once and look at the wound
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Cover the wound with a sterile dressing at once and look at the wound

Clinical Rationale: An open wound is covered with a sterile dressing at once and examined, so that the germs of the bed and the air do NOT enter it.

Key Clue: 45-year-old woman whose dressing has come off in the bed with the wound open

Priority Principle: Wound care / Dressing

Why Not Others: (a) A note at the round leaves the wound open for a long time; (b) A hand or a sheet on an open wound brings the germs of the ward into it; (c) The water of the ward is not clean for an open wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a wash seems the FIRST care of an open wound.

5-Second Recall: Dressing gir gayi aur ghaav khula = turant sterile dressing se dhako.

PNC Exam Pearl: An open wound is covered before the dressing round.

question: A nurse on the ward checks the machines at the start of the shift and finds that the suction machine used for a client does NOT pull. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the nurse of the next shift to look at the machine later
option_2: Note the fault in the ward book and wait for the engineer
option_3: Send the machine for repair and ask for a spare before the need comes
option_4: Keep the machine at the bed of the client who may need it
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Send the machine for repair and ask for a spare before the need comes

Clinical Rationale: A suction machine that does NOT pull is sent for repair and a spare is asked for at once, because the need for an airway can come at any hour of the shift.

Key Clue: suction machine that does NOT pull at the start of the shift of the ward

Priority Principle: Management / Ward machines

Why Not Others: (a) A word to the next shift passes the fault to others; (b) A note in the book leaves the ward without a suction for the shift; (d) A machine that does not work at the bed gives no help in the hour of need.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the ward book seems the proper place for a fault.

5-Second Recall: Suction machine kharab = turant repair bhejo aur spare maango.

PNC Exam Pearl: A machine is checked at the start of the shift and not in the hour of need.

question: A nurse must give a warm soak to the foot of a 60-year-old man on the ward who has a sore on the toe. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put the foot into the water and add hot water as it cools
option_2: Ask the man to tell when the water feels warm to him
option_3: Pour the water at the heat that feels warm to the hands
option_4: Check the heat of the water with the elbow and the skin of the foot
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check the heat of the water with the elbow and the skin of the foot

Clinical Rationale: The heat of the water is checked with the elbow and the skin of the foot before the foot goes in, because the skin of an old man with a sore feels less heat and burns easily.

Key Clue: warm soak for the foot of a 60-year-old man with a sore on the toe

Priority Principle: Safety / Heat on the skin

Why Not Others: (a) Hot water added during the soak burns the skin of the foot; (b) A man with a sore foot may not feel the heat of the water; (c) The hands of the nurse are harder than the skin of the foot of an old man.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the hands of the nurse seem the right test of the water.

5-Second Recall: Garam paani ki heat kohni aur pair ki chamdi se test karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Water for a soak is tested on the elbow and never on the hands alone.

question: A nurse must give an enema to a 50-year-old man on the ward who has had no stool for four days. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Check the order and the state of the man and warm the fluid to the right heat
option_2: Give the enema with the fluid at the heat of the room
option_3: Ask the man to hold the enema for an hour before he passes it
option_4: Give a strong drug for the stool and take the enema later
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check the order and the state of the man and warm the fluid to the right heat

Clinical Rationale: The order and the state of the man are checked and the fluid is warmed to body heat before the enema is given, so that the bowel is NOT harmed.

Key Clue: enema for a 50-year-old man who has had no stool for four days

Priority Principle: Procedure / Enema

Why Not Others: (b) A cool fluid in the bowel brings a cramp and a poor effect; (c) The enema is held for a few minutes and not for an hour; (d) A strong drug without an order comes before the enema that was ordered.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a long hold seems the sure way of an enema.

5-Second Recall: Enema se pehle order, client ki haalat aur paani ka tapman check karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The fluid of an enema is given at body heat.

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward who has a chest drain says that the pain in the chest is worse on taking a breath in, and the nurse feels a crackling under the skin at the neck. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put a warm pack on the chest and note the pain in the chart
option_2: Call the doctor at once and stay with the man while he is watched
option_3: Ask the man to take slow deep breaths and cough out the sputum
option_4: Clamp the chest drain and wait for the doctor's round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Call the doctor at once and stay with the man while he is watched

Clinical Rationale: A crackling under the skin of the neck in a man with a chest drain means that air is under the skin, so the doctor is called at once and the man is watched by the nurse.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man with a chest drain, pain on taking a breath in and a crackling under the skin at the neck

Priority Principle: ABC / Air under the skin

Why Not Others: (a) A warm pack and a note leave the air under the skin to spread; (c) Deep breaths and a cough push more air out of the lung; (d) A clamp on the drain holds the air inside the chest.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a warm pack seems the relief of a pain of the chest.

5-Second Recall: Chest tube aur gardan ki chamdi me kadkad = doctor turant bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Air that is felt under the skin of the neck is reported at once.

Reference Table: Primary acid-base disorders - Metabolic acidosis: Low pH | down HCO3 | DKA, diarrhoea; Metabolic alkalosis: High pH | up HCO3 | Vomiting, diuretics; Respiratory acidosis: Low pH | up PaCO2 | COPD, sedation; Respiratory alkalosis: High pH | down PaCO2 | Hyperventilation, anxiety.

question: A nurse must change the tracheostomy tube of a 55-year-old man on the ward who has had it for a month. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the man to take a deep breath while the old tube comes out
option_2: Take the old tube out at once and pass the fresh tube after it
option_3: Keep a fresh tube of the same size and the suction ready before the change
option_4: Give a drug for the pain and wait for the doctor to change the tube
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep a fresh tube of the same size and the suction ready before the change

Clinical Rationale: A fresh tube of the same size and the suction are kept ready before the old tube comes out, because the airway must NOT be left open without a tube of the right size.

Key Clue: tracheostomy tube of a 55-year-old man that must be changed after a month

Priority Principle: Procedure / Tracheostomy tube
