Why Not Others: (a) A deep breath at the hour of the change can push the old tube out of place; (b) An old tube taken out without a fresh one risks a blocked airway; (d) Waiting for the doctor with a blocked tube costs the airway.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the old tube seems the fault that must come out FIRST.

5-Second Recall: Tracheostomy tube badalne se pehle nayi tube aur suction taiyaar rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fresh tube of the same size is kept ready before the old tube moves.

question: A nurse checks the bottle of the chest drain of a 45-year-old man on the ward and sees that the water in the long tube has stopped moving up and down with the breath. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the drain out of the chest and put a dressing on the site
option_2: Look along the whole tube for a kink or a block and inform the doctor
option_3: Milk the tube hard with the fingers to move the water again
option_4: Ask the man to cough and to change his side on the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Look along the whole tube for a kink or a block and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Water that has stopped moving with the breath points to a kink or a block in the tube, so the whole tube is examined and the doctor is informed.

Key Clue: water in the long tube of the chest bottle of a 45-year-old man that has stopped moving with the breath

Priority Principle: ABC / Chest drain

Why Not Others: (a) A drain taken out of the chest without an order can let air into it; (c) Milking the tube hard can pull the lung and the chest drain; (d) A cough and a change of side do not open a tube that is blocked.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because milking the tube seems the work that brings the swing back.

5-Second Recall: Chest tube ka paani hilna band = tube me kink dhundo, doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The whole tube is followed from the chest to the bottle before the doctor is called.

question: A nurse on the ward has four clients, and one 55-year-old woman has had a bag of fluid run into her vein in half an hour and is now breathless with a wet cough. Which client should the nurse see FIRST?
option_1: The woman who is breathless with a wet cough after the fast fluid
option_2: The client who asks for a fresh glass of water
option_3: The client who wants the blanket to be folded
option_4: The client whose family asks about the ward bill
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The woman who is breathless with a wet cough after the fast fluid

Clinical Rationale: A woman who is breathless with a wet cough after a fast bag of fluid is overloaded with fluid, so she is seen before every other client on the ward.

Key Clue: four clients and one 55-year-old woman who is breathless with a wet cough after a bag of fluid in half an hour

Priority Principle: ABC / Fluid overload

Why Not Others: (b) The glass of water can wait for the hour round; (c) The blanket is a small matter of the room; (d) The ward bill is a desk matter.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the water seems the need the nurse can meet fastest.

5-Second Recall: Aadhe ghante me pura bag aur saans phoolna = pehle usi ko dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fast drip is watched for a wet cough and a short breath.

question: A nurse must give a drug into the muscle of a 55-year-old woman on the ward who had her right breast removed two years ago. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the woman to choose the arm that she prefers for the needle
option_2: Give the injection into the right arm at the place of the old operation
option_3: Give the injection into the right thigh of the woman at once
option_4: Ask about the side of the operation and choose the left arm for the injection
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Ask about the side of the operation and choose the left arm for the injection

Clinical Rationale: The side of the operation is asked about and the left arm is chosen, because the arm on the side of the removed breast drains poorly and swells after injections.

Key Clue: 55-year-old woman who had her right breast removed two years ago and needs a drug into the muscle

Priority Principle: Procedure / Injection site

Why Not Others: (a) The site is chosen by the state of the woman and not by her wish alone; (b) An injection in the arm of the operated side brings swelling of the arm; (c) The thigh of a woman who can have the left arm is not the first choice.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the operated arm seems the same as any other arm.

5-Second Recall: Breast removed ki taraf wale haath me injection nahi - doosra haath.

PNC Exam Pearl: The history of breast surgery is asked before the site is chosen.

question: A nurse in the child ward must take blood from the arm of a 3-year-old child for a test, and the mother is with the child. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a drug to make the child sleep for the test
option_2: Ask the mother to leave the room while the needle goes in
option_3: Take the blood with the child held down by the nurse alone
option_4: Explain the step to the mother and hold the child still with a helper
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Explain the step to the mother and hold the child still with a helper

Clinical Rationale: The step is explained to the mother and the child is held still with a helper, so that one clean prick is made and the child is NOT held down by force.

Key Clue: 3-year-old child who needs blood taken from the arm with the mother near the bed

Priority Principle: Procedure / Blood from a child

Why Not Others: (a) A drug for sleep for a simple test is not ordered; (b) A mother sent out of the room leaves the child with fear and no comfort; (c) A child held by one person moves and takes more pricks.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the mother out of the room seems the calm way of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Bachche ka blood se pehle maa ko samjhao aur helper se pakadwao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A child is held by the right number of hands and not by force.

question: A nurse hears a sound from the pump that runs a drug into the vein of a 50-year-old man on the ward and sees a block message on the screen. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the line out of the arm and put a fresh line in the other arm
option_2: Press the button of the pump again and again to clear the alarm
option_3: Look at the site of the line and the whole tube for a kink or a swelling
option_4: Stop the pump and give the drug into the muscle as ordered
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Look at the site of the line and the whole tube for a kink or a swelling

Clinical Rationale: A block message on the pump is answered by looking at the site and the whole tube for a kink or a swelling, because the alarm tells of a fault of the line and NOT of the machine.

Key Clue: pump running a drug into the vein of a 50-year-old man with a block message on the screen

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Line and pump

Why Not Others: (a) A fresh line in the other arm is a step after the fault is found; (b) Pressing the button again sends the drug against a block; (d) A drug ordered into the vein is not given into the muscle.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the button seems the answer to the sound of the pump.

5-Second Recall: Pump 'block' bole = pehle line aur site dekho, button dabate raho mat.

PNC Exam Pearl: An alarm of a pump is answered at the arm of the client first.

question: A 50-year-old man on the ward has a drain in the abdomen that has NOT drained for a whole shift, and he now has pain with a hard and distended belly. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Push the tube of the drain in a little so that it drains again
option_2: Look at the drain and the tube and inform the doctor at once
option_3: Change the dressing of the site and put a warm pack on the belly
option_4: Note the dry drain in the chart and wait for the doctor's round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Look at the drain and the tube and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A drain that has stopped with pain and a hard belly points to a block, so the drain and the tube are examined and the doctor is informed at once.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man with a drain in the abdomen that has NOT drained for a shift, with pain and a hard distended belly

Priority Principle: Safety / Drain

Why Not Others: (a) Pushing the tube in takes the germs into the wound; (c) A warm pack hides the state of the belly and the drain; (d) Waiting for the round lets the belly and the pain get worse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a push seems the way to make a drain work.

5-Second Recall: Drain band aur pet kadak-dard = drain check karo, doctor ko turant batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A drain that stops working is reported with the state of the belly.

question: A nurse must give a drug into the muscle of a 40-year-old man on the ward who is very restless and shouts at the staff. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Call a helper, speak to the man calmly and give the drug with care
option_2: Ask two staff to hold the man down and give the drug at once
option_3: Wait for the man to fall asleep and give the drug after that
option_4: Leave the drug aside and lock the door of the man's room
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Call a helper, speak to the man calmly and give the drug with care

Clinical Rationale: A helper is called and the man is spoken to calmly before the drug is given, so that the man is safe and the staff are safe at the same time.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man in the ward who is very restless and shouts at the staff and needs a drug into the muscle

Priority Principle: Safety / Care of a restless client

Why Not Others: (b) Holding the man down before any word raises the struggle and the harm; (c) Waiting for sleep leaves the man without the ordered drug; (d) A locked door raises the fear of the man.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a firm hold seems the fast way to keep the ward safe.

5-Second Recall: Bechain client ko pehle shaant awaaz me samjhao, madad saath rakho, phir dawa.

PNC Exam Pearl: The words of the nurse are used before the hands of the staff.

question: A nurse must take the weight of a 60-year-old woman on the ward who cannot stand and has a drip in the arm. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the weight of the last month and continue the round
option_2: Stand the woman up on the floor scale with a helper on each side
option_3: Ask the woman to step on the scale and hold the drip stand
option_4: Use a chair or bed scale and take the weight with a helper
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Use a chair or bed scale and take the weight with a helper

Clinical Rationale: A woman who cannot stand is weighed on a chair or bed scale with a helper, so that the drip is kept safe and no fall takes place.

Key Clue: 60-year-old woman who cannot stand and has a drip in the arm and needs to be weighed

Priority Principle: Procedure / Client weight

Why Not Others: (a) An old weight is not the weight of today; (b) Standing on the floor scale brings a fall in a woman who cannot stand; (c) Holding the drip stand pulls the line out of the arm.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the floor scale seems the usual way of a weight.

5-Second Recall: Khadi nahi ho sakti = chair ya bed scale, helper ke saath wazan lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The way of taking the weight is chosen by the state of the client.

question: A nurse takes a vial of a drug from the fridge for an injection ordered for a 45-year-old woman on the ward and sees that the fluid in it is cloudy with small specks. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Shake the vial well and give the drug as ordered
option_2: Warm the vial in the hands and give the drug from it
option_3: Keep the vial aside and take a fresh vial after checking the order
option_4: Put the vial back in the fridge and give the drug later
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the vial aside and take a fresh vial after checking the order

Clinical Rationale: A clear drug that has become cloudy with specks has gone bad, so the vial is kept aside and a fresh vial is taken after the order is checked.

Key Clue: vial of a drug from the fridge with a cloudy fluid and small specks for an injection ordered for a 45-year-old woman

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Bad drug

Why Not Others: (a) Shaking the vial mixes the specks into the drug; (b) A warm vial with specks still holds the specks; (d) A vial put back spoils the drug of the fridge for others.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a shake seems the way to mix a drug well.

5-Second Recall: Dawa me dhabbe ya dhundh = wo vial phenko, nayi vial lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every drug that enters the body is checked for colour and specks before it is drawn.

question: A nurse must take blood from a 60-year-old man on the ward for a blood sugar test, and the man has a drip in the right arm. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the blood from the right arm above the site of the drip
option_2: Take the blood from the left arm and keep the drip arm for the fluid
option_3: Take the blood from the same line as the fluid that is running
option_4: Stop the drip for an hour and take the blood after that time
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Take the blood from the left arm and keep the drip arm for the fluid

Clinical Rationale: The blood is taken from the left arm and the arm with the drip is kept for the fluid, so that the sample is NOT mixed with the fluid that runs into the vein.

Key Clue: blood for a blood sugar test from a 60-year-old man who has a drip in the right arm

Priority Principle: Procedure / Blood sample

Why Not Others: (a) Blood taken above a running drip is mixed with the fluid of the drip; (c) A sample from the fluid line gives a wrong value of the sugar; (d) Stopping an ordered drip for an hour harms the client.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the arm with the drip seems the arm that is ready for a needle.

5-Second Recall: Drip wale haath se khoon nahi - doosre haath se sample lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A blood sample is never taken from a vein that carries a running fluid.

question: A nurse at a sub-centre has run a load of the autoclave in the morning for a client who comes to the OPD. Which action should the nurse take FIRST with the load?
option_1: Note the date and the number of the load in the book and dry the packs
option_2: Give the packs to the families of the village for use at home
option_3: Use the packs at once while they are still warm and wet
option_4: Keep the packs in the box with the dirty gloves of the centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Note the date and the number of the load in the book and dry the packs

Clinical Rationale: The date and the number of the load are written in the book and the packs are dried, so that the sterile packs are known and are kept dry.

Key Clue: load of the autoclave that has run in the morning at the sub-centre

Priority Principle: Infection control / Load record

Why Not Others: (b) Packs given to the families are not used under the eye of the nurse; (c) A wet pack lets the germs of the air pass through it; (d) A pack kept with dirty gloves is no longer sterile.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a warm pack seems the pack that is ready for use.

5-Second Recall: Autoclave ke load ki date aur number book me likho, packs sukhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A wet sterile pack is kept as a pack that is not sterile.

question: A nurse who is passing the room of a 65-year-old man on the ward sees him trying to get down from the bed to the floor without help. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put the rail of the bed up and leave him for a short time
option_2: Call from the door and tell him to wait for the round
option_3: Give him the bell and go to the next client on the ward
option_4: Go to the man at once and help him to the chair with support
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Go to the man at once and help him to the chair with support

Clinical Rationale: A man who is getting down without help is at once helped to the chair with support, so that a fall is stopped before it happens.

Key Clue: 65-year-old man who tries to get down from the bed to the floor without help

Priority Principle: Safety / Fall

Why Not Others: (a) A rail up and a leave keep the man in the bed against his wish; (b) A call from the door is too late for a man who is already moving; (c) A bell in the hand and a walk away leave the man alone on the edge of the bed.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a call seems the quick guard of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Client khud utar raha hai = turant ja kar sahaara do.

PNC Exam Pearl: The care of a fall begins with the feet of the nurse at the bed.

question: A nurse checks the weighing scale on the ward before the weight of a client and sees that the pointer does NOT come back to the zero mark. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Set the scale to the zero mark before the client stands on it
option_2: Note the weight as it reads and write the number in the chart
option_3: Step on the scale to test it before the client is weighed
option_4: Use the scale of the next ward for the weight of the client
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Set the scale to the zero mark before the client stands on it

Clinical Rationale: A scale that does NOT come back to zero is set to the zero mark before the client stands on it, because the reading of a scale that is NOT at zero is wrong.

Key Clue: weighing scale in the ward with a pointer that does NOT come back to the zero mark

Priority Principle: Procedure / Weight

Why Not Others: (b) A weight from a scale that is not at zero is a false number; (c) A step of the nurse on the scale does not set it to zero; (d) The scale of the next ward is a change of place and not of the worth of the machine.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a step on the scale seems the way to test it.

5-Second Recall: Scale zero par nahi aa raha = pehle zero karo, phir wazan lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The scale is set to zero at the start of every weight.

question: A 70-year-old woman on the ward has a drip in the arm and says that the needle site is painful, and the nurse sees that the fluid has stopped running. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Open the clamp wide so that the fluid runs fast and opens the line
option_2: Look at the site and the tube for a kink or a swelling before the flow is touched
option_3: Raise the bottle of the fluid higher on the stand at once
option_4: Ask the woman to move the arm about till the fluid runs again
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Look at the site and the tube for a kink or a swelling before the flow is touched

Clinical Rationale: A painful site with a flow that has stopped is examined with the tube for a kink or a swelling before the clamp is touched, because a fast flow into a vein that has gone harms the arm.

Key Clue: 70-year-old woman with a drip in the arm, pain at the site and a flow that has stopped running

Priority Principle: Safety / Drip line

Why Not Others: (a) A wide clamp pushes the fluid into the tissue of the arm; (c) A higher bottle does not set right the site that is painful; (d) Moving the arm about can push the needle through the vein.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a wide clamp seems the way to open a line that has stopped.

5-Second Recall: Drip ruk gaya aur jagah dard = pehle site aur line dekho, clamp mat kholo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A stopped drip is examined before the flow is opened wide.

question: A nurse checks the colostomy bag of a 50-year-old man on the ward and sees that the bag is puffed up with air and stands out from the skin. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put a fresh bag on the skin without opening the old one
option_2: Press the bag against the belly so that the air goes back inside
option_3: Open the small door at the top of the bag to let the air out
option_4: Make a small hole in the bag with a needle
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Open the small door at the top of the bag to let the air out

Clinical Rationale: A bag that is puffed with air is let down by the small door at the top, so that the bag lies flat on the skin and does NOT pull at the opening.

Key Clue: colostomy bag of a 50-year-old man that is puffed up with air and stands out from the skin

Priority Principle: Skin safety / Colostomy bag

Why Not Others: (a) A fresh bag over the puffed one leaves the air inside it; (b) A press on the bag pushes the air and the stool back into the opening; (d) A hole with a needle harms the bag and lets the stool out.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a press on the bag seems the way to empty the air.

5-Second Recall: Bag hawa se phoola = upar ka chhota darwaza kholo, hawa nikaalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The small door at the top of the bag is made for the air of the bowel.

question: A nurse opens the cold box at a village session for the child who attends the clinic and finds that the thermometer inside reads 10 degrees Celsius. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take out the water of the melted ice and put in fresh ice packs
option_2: Note the reading of the thermometer and continue the session
option_3: Keep the vaccines in the shade of the tree till the session ends
option_4: Freeze the vaccine vials at once so that they are cold again
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Take out the water of the melted ice and put in fresh ice packs

Clinical Rationale: A cold box that reads 10 degrees has lost the cold chain, so the water of the melted ice is taken out and fresh ice packs are put in at once.

Key Clue: cold box at a village session whose thermometer reads 10 degrees Celsius

Priority Principle: Cold chain / Cold box

Why Not Others: (b) A note and a session leave the vaccine warm for the hours of the work; (c) The shade of a tree does not keep the vaccine between 2 and 8 degrees; (d) A frozen vaccine loses its potency and is thrown away.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the shade of a tree seems the cool place of a hot day.

5-Second Recall: Cold box 10 degree = pighla paani nikaalo, naye ice packs daalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The vaccine is kept between 2 and 8 degrees from the centre to the child.

question: A nurse must give mouth care to a 60-year-old man on the ward who is on oxygen by mask. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Turn the oxygen off for the whole hour of the mouth care
option_2: Take the mask off and give the care without looking at the oxygen
option_3: Give the mouth care with the mask in its place on the face
option_4: Ask the man if he can keep the mask off for a few minutes for the care
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Ask the man if he can keep the mask off for a few minutes for the care

Clinical Rationale: The man is asked if he can keep the mask off for a few minutes and the care is given with the oxygen ready to go back, so that he is NOT left short of air.

Key Clue: mouth care for a 60-year-old man who is on oxygen by mask

Priority Principle: Mouth care / Oxygen

Why Not Others: (a) An hour without the ordered oxygen harms a man who needs it; (b) A mask taken off without a look at the state of the man leaves him short of air; (c) Care with the mask in place does not clean the mouth inside.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because mouth care seems the FIRST duty of a shift.

5-Second Recall: Oxygen mask wale ka muh ki safai = thodi der mask hatao, oxygen paas rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The care is short and the oxygen goes back on at once.

question: A nurse must put on sterile gloves for the care of a wound of a 45-year-old man on the ward. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put on the gloves without the wash because the gloves are sterile
option_2: Open the packet of the gloves on the wet trolley of the ward
option_3: Wash the hands and open the packet of the gloves on a clean dry surface
option_4: Take the gloves out of the packet and put them on the bed side
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Wash the hands and open the packet of the gloves on a clean dry surface

Clinical Rationale: The hands are washed and the packet is opened on a clean dry surface before the gloves are put on, so that the gloves stay sterile to the last finger.

Key Clue: sterile gloves to be put on for the care of the wound of a 45-year-old man

Priority Principle: Procedure / Sterile gloves

Why Not Others: (a) Washing the hands is kept even under sterile gloves; (b) A wet trolley wets the packet and the gloves inside it; (d) Gloves on the bed side take the germs of the bed.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the sterile gloves seem the whole guard of the hand.

5-Second Recall: Sterile gloves se pehle haath dhoyo aur packet saaf-sukhi jagah kholo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A wet surface turns a sterile packet into a wet packet.

question: A 55-year-old man on the ward with a nasogastric tube says that his throat is sore and that it burns when he swallows his own spit. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the tube out of the nose and pass a fresh tube at once
option_2: Look at the tube and the mark, give mouth care and inform the nurse in charge
option_3: Ask the man to drink a glass of cold water to ease the throat
option_4: Note the sore throat in the chart and give the feed as ordered
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Look at the tube and the mark, give mouth care and inform the nurse in charge

Clinical Rationale: A sore throat with a burning on swallowing in a man with a nasogastric tube is examined with the mark, and mouth care is given while the nurse in charge is informed.

Key Clue: 55-year-old man with a nasogastric tube who has a sore throat and burning on swallowing the spit

Priority Principle: Care / Nasogastric tube

Why Not Others: (a) A fresh tube at once may sit in the same sore place; (c) A drink of cold water eases the throat for a short time and does not treat the cause; (d) A feed down a tube that burns the throat makes the sore worse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a fresh tube seems the answer to a sore throat.

5-Second Recall: Nose tube se gale me jalan = tube-mark dekho, muh ki safai do, in-charge ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Mouth care is the simple help of a client with a nasogastric tube.

question: A nurse must give back care to a 70-year-old man on the ward who cannot turn himself. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Rub the skin over the bones of the back with a hard hand
option_2: Put the lotion on the man's back as it lies on the shelf
option_3: Warm the hands and the lotion and turn the man on to the side
option_4: Give the back care with the man flat on his back
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Warm the hands and the lotion and turn the man on to the side

Clinical Rationale: The hands and the lotion are warmed and the man is turned on to the side before the back care, so that the skin is safe and the man is at ease.

Key Clue: back care for a 70-year-old man who cannot turn himself

Priority Principle: Procedure / Back care

Why Not Others: (a) A hard rub over the bones of the back harms the skin; (b) Cold lotion on the back of an old man is a shock to the skin; (d) Care with the man flat does not reach the skin of the back.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a hard rub seems the way to bring the blood to the skin.

5-Second Recall: Kamar ki care se pehle haath aur lotion garam karo, client ko karwat do.

PNC Exam Pearl: The skin over the bones of the back is examined with the back care.

question: A 50-year-old man on the ward is to have a lumbar puncture, and the doctor has NOT yet come. Which action has the HIGHEST priority for the nurse now?
option_1: Put a pillow under the man's head and keep him flat on his back
option_2: Give the man a drink of water so that he is NOT thirsty during the test
option_3: Ask the man to sign the consent form after the test is done
option_4: Ask the man to pass urine and place him on the side with the back curved
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Ask the man to pass urine and place him on the side with the back curved

Clinical Rationale: Before a lumbar puncture the man is asked to pass urine and is placed on the side with the back curved, so that the space between the bones is open and the step is safe.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man who is to have a lumbar puncture and waits for the doctor

Priority Principle: Procedure / Lumbar puncture

Why Not Others: (a) A pillow under the head and a flat back close the space between the bones; (b) A drink of water is not given before a step of this kind; (c) The consent form is signed before the step and not after it.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the consent form seems the FIRST duty of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Spinal test se pehle: peshaab karao aur karwat me back gol karao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The position of the client opens the space for the spinal needle.

question: A nurse must pass a catheter into the bladder of a 25-year-old woman in labour on the ward who cannot pass urine. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the area from the front to the back and keep the field free of germs
option_2: Put the catheter in fast so that the labour is NOT held up
option_3: Use the same catheter for a second try if the FIRST does NOT pass
option_4: Empty the bladder by pressing the lower abdomen of the woman
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the area from the front to the back and keep the field free of germs

Clinical Rationale: The area is cleaned from the front to the back and the field is kept free of germs before the catheter goes in, so that the bladder does NOT take an infection.

Key Clue: catheter to be passed into the bladder of a 25-year-old woman in labour who cannot pass urine

Priority Principle: Procedure / Bladder catheter

Why Not Others: (b) A fast step without the clean field takes the germs into the bladder; (c) A second try with the same catheter pushes the germs inside; (d) A press on a full bladder in labour harms the uterus and the bladder.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the same catheter seems a saving of the stock.

5-Second Recall: Catheter se pehle aage se peeche saaf karo, field sterile rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fresh catheter is used for every try at the bladder.

question: A 75-year-old man on the ward has had the drip needle taken out of the arm, and the site now has a bruise with a swelling and a slow ooze of blood. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Rub the site with a warm hand to spread the blood under the skin
option_2: Press on the site with a clean pad and put a cold pack over it
option_3: Put a warm pack on the site and raise the arm on the bed
option_4: Note the bruise in the chart and cover the site with a dry pad
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Press on the site with a clean pad and put a cold pack over it

Clinical Rationale: A bruise with a swelling and an ooze after a needle is pressed with a clean pad and cooled with a cold pack, so that the bleeding under the skin stops.

Key Clue: 75-year-old man with a bruise and a swelling at the site of a drip needle and a slow ooze of blood

Priority Principle: Safety / Needle site

Why Not Others: (a) A rub spreads the blood under the skin and makes the bruise larger; (c) A warm pack brings more blood to the site that is oozing; (d) A dry pad without a press leaves the ooze to go on.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a warm pack seems the comfort of a bruised arm.

5-Second Recall: Needle nikalne ke baad khoon rukna nahi = saaf pad se dabao, thanda pack lagao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A press on the site comes before any pack is put on it.

question: A nurse must give 30 units of insulin to a 45-year-old woman on the ward, and the only syringe on the trolley has a scale of 100 units marked in millilitres. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Draw 30 marks of the millilitre syringe and give the dose
option_2: Take a syringe that is marked in units of insulin before the dose is drawn
option_3: Draw the dose by eye from the vial of insulin into the syringe
option_4: Ask another nurse to draw the dose and give it to the woman
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Take a syringe that is marked in units of insulin before the dose is drawn

Clinical Rationale: Insulin is drawn in a syringe that is marked in units of insulin, so the right syringe is taken before the dose is drawn.

Key Clue: 30 units of insulin to be drawn with only a syringe of 100 units marked in millilitres

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Insulin syringe

Why Not Others: (a) A millilitre syringe has no marks of units of insulin and gives a wrong dose; (c) A dose drawn by eye is not measured at all; (d) A second nurse with the wrong syringe gives the same wrong dose.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the marks of the syringe seem the marks of the dose.

5-Second Recall: Insulin ka dose units wali syringe me hi naapo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Insulin and its syringe are a pair that is never mixed with another.

question: A nurse on the ward finds that the bottle of the chest drain of a 60-year-old man has fallen on the floor and is broken. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Lift the end of the tube above the man's chest and hold it there
option_2: Clamp the tube at once and call the doctor from the desk
option_3: Put the end of the tube into a clean bottle of sterile water below the chest
option_4: Take the drain out of the chest and put a dressing on the site
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Put the end of the tube into a clean bottle of sterile water below the chest

Clinical Rationale: The end of the tube is put into a clean bottle of sterile water below the level of the chest at once, so that no air enters the chest and the fluid can drain.

Key Clue: bottle of the chest drain of a 60-year-old man broken on the floor of the ward

Priority Principle: ABC / Chest drain

Why Not Others: (a) An end held above the chest lets the fluid run back inside; (b) A clamp on the tube can press air inside the chest; (d) A drain taken out without an order can let air into the chest.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a clamp seems the sure stop of air in the chest.

5-Second Recall: Chest tube ki bottle toot gayi = tube ka sira neeche sterile paani me daalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A bottle that is broken is replaced by a bottle of water below the chest.

question: A nurse must keep a watch on the urine of a 70-year-old man on the ward who has a urinary catheter, and the order is to report a fall of the output below 30 millilitres per hour. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give more water to the man and wait for the urine to rise
option_2: Measure the urine of the whole day and report at the end of it
option_3: Empty the bag every four hours and note the amount in the chart
option_4: Measure the urine every hour and report the FIRST fall below the mark
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Measure the urine every hour and report the FIRST fall below the mark

Clinical Rationale: The urine is measured every hour and the FIRST fall below 30 millilitres per hour is reported at once, because a low output in a man of 70 years is a sign of a low flow of blood.

Key Clue: 70-year-old man with a urinary catheter and an order to report a fall of the urine below 30 millilitres per hour

Priority Principle: Lab / Urine output

Why Not Others: (a) More water does not raise the urine of a man whose kidneys are short of blood; (b) A report at the end of the day is far too late for a low output; (c) Emptying the bag every four hours hides the fall of an hour.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the whole day seems the right measure of a balance.

5-Second Recall: Hourly urine 30 mL se kam = turant doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fall of the urine of an hour is reported in the same hour.

question: A nurse must change the colostomy bag of a 50-year-old man on the ward that has been on the skin for three days. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the bag off with care and look at the skin round the opening
option_2: Pull the bag off fast so that the skin is NOT pulled with it
option_3: Put the fresh bag over the old one without taking it off
option_4: Wash the skin with spirit and fit the fresh bag at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Take the bag off with care and look at the skin round the opening

Clinical Rationale: The bag is taken off with care and the skin round the opening is examined, so that a sore of the skin is found before a fresh bag goes on.

Key Clue: colostomy bag of a 50-year-old man that has been on the skin for three days

Priority Principle: Skin safety / Colostomy bag

Why Not Others: (b) A fast pull takes the top skin off and makes a sore; (c) A fresh bag over the old one hides the skin and lets a sore grow; (d) Spirit on the skin round the opening dries and harms it.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a fast pull seems the way to save the man the pain.

5-Second Recall: Bag badalte waqt dheere se hatao, chamdi dekho, phir naya bag.

PNC Exam Pearl: The skin round the opening is examined at every change of the bag.

question: A nurse is to give a drug into the vein of a 55-year-old man on the ward through a line that has a filter, and the filter is wet with a white deposit on it. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the filter off the line and give the drug without it
option_2: Push the drug through the filter so that the deposit goes into the man
option_3: Shake the filter and continue with the drug as ordered
option_4: Change the set with the filter before the drug is given and inform the nurse in charge
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Change the set with the filter before the drug is given and inform the nurse in charge

Clinical Rationale: A filter with a white deposit on it is changed with the whole set before the drug goes in, because the deposit may be the drug itself or a germ.

Key Clue: line with a filter for a drug into the vein of a 55-year-old man and a filter that is wet with a white deposit

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Line and filter

Why Not Others: (a) A filter taken off takes away the guard of the line; (b) A push through a blocked filter sends the deposit into the vein; (c) Shaking the filter does not clear the deposit from it.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a shake seems the way to clear a wet filter.

5-Second Recall: Filter par safed jama = set badlo, phir dawa do.

PNC Exam Pearl: A filter that is wet or coated is changed with the set.

question: A 25-year-old woman in labour on the ward has a drip that makes the pains, and the nurse notes that the uterus stays hard and does NOT relax between the pains. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Stop the drip of the drug, turn the woman on the side and inform the doctor
option_2: Open the drip faster so that the labour is over soon
option_3: Ask the woman to push with every pain of the uterus
option_4: Note the state of the uterus in the chart and watch for an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stop the drip of the drug, turn the woman on the side and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A uterus that stays hard and does NOT relax between the pains means too much of the drug of the pains, so the drip is stopped, the woman is turned on the side and the doctor is informed.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman in labour on a drip that makes the pains and a uterus that stays hard between the pains

Priority Principle: Safety / Mother and fetus

Why Not Others: (b) A faster drip takes the uterus into a state that harms the baby; (c) A push against a uterus that does not relax harms the uterus; (d) An hour of watching lets the uterus and the baby come to harm.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a faster drip seems the quick end of the labour.

5-Second Recall: Womb dard ke beech relax nahi = dawa ka drip band karo, karwat do, doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: The uterus is felt between the pains at every watch of a labour on a drip.

question: A nurse must give foot care to a 60-year-old man on the ward who has diabetes. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Cut the nails of the toes short and round at the corners
option_2: Look at the skin between the toes and the colour of both feet
option_3: Soak the feet in hot water for half an hour and rub them dry
option_4: Put a warm bag on the feet so that the blood comes to them
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Look at the skin between the toes and the colour of both feet

Clinical Rationale: The skin between the toes and the colour of the feet are examined FIRST, because a man with diabetes may have a sore that he cannot feel.

Key Clue: foot care for a 60-year-old man who has diabetes

Priority Principle: Foot care / Diabetes

Why Not Others: (a) A nail cut short at the corners cuts the skin of a numb toe; (c) Hot water on a numb foot burns it before any pain is felt; (d) A warm bag on a numb foot brings a burn of the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a warm soak seems the comfort of tired feet.

5-Second Recall: Sugar wale client ke pair pehle dekho - naakhoon chhota mat kaato.

PNC Exam Pearl: A sore of the foot in a client with diabetes is found by looking and not by feeling.

question: A nurse is to move a 45-year-old man on the ward who has a nasogastric tube and a drip in the arm to another ward. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the man to hold the bottle of the drip during the move
option_2: Take the tube and the drip out and put them in again in the new ward
option_3: Close both the lines and check the marks before the man is moved
option_4: Leave the tube and the drip open and move the man with the trolley
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Close both the lines and check the marks before the man is moved

Clinical Rationale: Both the lines are closed and the marks are checked before the move, so that the feed does NOT run out and the drip does NOT pull on the arm.

Key Clue: 45-year-old man with a nasogastric tube and a drip in the arm who is to be moved to another ward

Priority Principle: Safety / Client move

Why Not Others: (a) A bottle held by the man pulls the line and wets the bed; (b) A tube and a line put in again at the new ward take two steps where none are needed; (d) An open tube and line spill the feed and the fluid on the way.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the bottle in the man's hand seems the easy way of a move.

5-Second Recall: Move se pehle dono line band karo aur nishaan check karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every line of a client is closed and checked before a move.

question: A nurse finds an 80-year-old woman on the ward who does NOT answer the call of the nurse, and the hearing aid lies on the table beside the bed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Write the words on a paper and show them to the woman
option_2: Shout into the ear of the woman so that she hears the nurse
option_3: Put the aid in the ear, switch it on and speak to the woman face to face
option_4: Note in the chart that the woman does NOT answer and go on
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Put the aid in the ear, switch it on and speak to the woman face to face

Clinical Rationale: The aid is put in the ear and switched on and the nurse speaks face to face, so that the hearing of the woman is restored before any other way of talking is used.

Key Clue: 80-year-old woman on the ward who does NOT answer with the hearing aid lying on the table

Priority Principle: Care of the old / Hearing

Why Not Others: (a) A paper is a help after the aid is set right; (b) A shout into the ear of an old woman is heard as noise and fear; (d) A note without a try at the aid leaves the woman cut off from the ward.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a loud voice seems the answer to a deaf ear.

5-Second Recall: Budhiya jawab nahi de rahi = hearing aid pehno, saamne se baat karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: An aid that lies on the table gives no hearing to the woman.

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward who has a line in the hand must be taken to another room for a test. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the needle out of the hand and put it in again after the test
option_2: Close the line, cap the end and keep the site clean and covered
option_3: Leave the line open so that the air does NOT go into the vein
option_4: Ask the man to hold the line above the head during the test
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Close the line, cap the end and keep the site clean and covered

Clinical Rationale: The line is closed and the end is capped and the site is kept clean and covered before the man is taken for the test, so that the line stays free of germs and of air.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man with a line in the hand who is to be taken to another room for a test

Priority Principle: Safety / Line in the hand

Why Not Others: (a) A fresh needle after the test takes a second step that is not needed; (c) A line left open lets the blood flow out and the air go in; (d) A line held above the head pulls at the site of the hand.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because an open line seems the way to keep the line ready.

5-Second Recall: Line ko band karo, cap lagao, site saaf aur dhaki rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A line is closed and capped whenever the client leaves the ward.

question: A nurse must take the pulse of a 60-year-old man on the ward whose beat is NOT regular. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Count the pulse for a full minute and note both the rate and the rhythm
option_2: Count the pulse for fifteen seconds and multiply the number by four
option_3: Count the pulse for ten seconds and note the number in the chart
option_4: Take the pulse of the wrist for a minute and wait for the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Count the pulse for a full minute and note both the rate and the rhythm

Clinical Rationale: A beat that is NOT regular is counted for a full minute with the rhythm noted, because a short count hides the missed beats of the wrist.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man with a pulse that is NOT regular

Priority Principle: Procedure / Pulse

Why Not Others: (b) A count of fifteen seconds does not show the missed beats of the pulse; (c) A count of ten seconds is too short for a beat that misses; (d) A count for a minute without the rhythm leaves out the state of the beat.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because fifteen seconds seems the fast count of a busy round.

5-Second Recall: Pulse beghair ho to poora ek minute gino, rate aur rhythm dono likho.

PNC Exam Pearl: An irregular pulse is counted for a full minute and felt for the rhythm.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse checks the urine bag of a 70-year-old man on the ward and sees that the urine is dark with a red tinge one hour after the catheter was put in. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give more water to the man so that the urine becomes clear
option_2: Take the catheter out at once and ask the man to pass urine himself
option_3: Wash the catheter with saline and open the flow wider
option_4: Note the colour and the amount and inform the doctor at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Note the colour and the amount and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A red tinge in the urine soon after a catheter has gone in points to a small injury of the urinary tract, so the colour and the amount are noted and the doctor is informed.

Key Clue: urine that is dark with a red tinge in the bag of a 70-year-old man one hour after the catheter went in

Priority Principle: Safety / Urinary catheter

Why Not Others: (a) More water does not treat an injury of the urinary tract; (b) A catheter taken out at once may need a fresh and more harmful try; (c) A wash and a wider flow push more blood out of the injured place.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a wash of the catheter seems the cleaning of the bladder.

5-Second Recall: Catheter ke baad peshaab me laal = doctor ko turant batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The first urine after a catheter is examined for blood and for the amount.

question: A 60-year-old woman on the ward has a fresh wound of the abdomen with a drain, and the nurse notes that the dressing is soaked through with a blood-stained fluid in one hour. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put a warm pack over the dressing and note the hour in the chart
option_2: Take the dressing off and look at the wound under a light
option_3: Reinforce the dressing with a fresh pad and inform the doctor at once
option_4: Change the whole dressing and fit a tight bandage over the wound
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Reinforce the dressing with a fresh pad and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A dressing that is soaked through in an hour is reinforced with a fresh pad and the doctor is informed at once, because a blood-stained fluid that comes fast points to bleeding.

Key Clue: 60-year-old woman with a fresh wound of the abdomen and a drain whose dressing is soaked through in one hour

Priority Principle: Bleeding / Dressing

Why Not Others: (a) A warm pack over the dressing hides the bleeding that goes on; (b) A dressing taken off under a light opens the wound to the air; (d) A tight bandage over the wound presses the fresh flesh and the drain.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a look at the wound seems the careful step of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Ek ghante me dressing bheeg gayi = upar se pad lagao, doctor ko turant batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A soaked dressing is reinforced and reported before it is changed.

question: A 70-year-old man on the ward who cannot hold his urine has red skin with a rash on the buttocks and the upper legs. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wash the skin with soap and water after every pad is changed
option_2: Clean the skin with warm water, dry it well and use a cream that guards the skin
option_3: Keep a rubber sheet under the man so that the bed stays dry
option_4: Put a thick pad between the legs and change it once in a shift
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clean the skin with warm water, dry it well and use a cream that guards the skin

Clinical Rationale: Red skin with a rash from urine is cleaned with warm water, dried well and guarded with a cream, so that the skin is NOT further harmed by the wet.

Key Clue: 70-year-old man who cannot hold his urine with red skin and a rash on the buttocks and the upper legs

Priority Principle: Skin safety / Skin care

Why Not Others: (a) A soap wash after every pad takes the oil of the skin away; (c) A rubber sheet holds the wet against the skin; (d) A pad changed once in a shift keeps the urine on the skin for hours.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a rubber sheet seems the clean way to keep a bed dry.

5-Second Recall: Peshaab ki laali = neem-garam paani se saaf karo, sukhao, cream lagao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The skin is kept dry and guarded at every change of the pad.

question: A nurse must check the skin of an 80-year-old woman on the ward who has nasal prongs for oxygen. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Look at the skin behind the ears and over the bridge of the nose and check the press of the prongs
option_2: Clean the nose of the woman with the water of the ward at once
option_3: Take the prongs off and give the oxygen by a mask for the rest of the day
option_4: Put a soft pad under the prongs and continue the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Look at the skin behind the ears and over the bridge of the nose and check the press of the prongs

Clinical Rationale: The skin behind the ears and over the bridge of the nose is examined and the press of the prongs is checked, because a press that lasts for hours brings a sore of the skin.

Key Clue: 80-year-old woman with nasal prongs for oxygen whose skin must be checked

Priority Principle: Skin safety / Oxygen prongs

Why Not Others: (b) Cleaning the nose does not look at the skin where the prongs press; (c) A change to the mask is a fresh order and not a check of the skin; (d) A pad under the prongs without a look at the skin hides a sore that has begun.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a soft pad seems the whole guard of the skin.

5-Second Recall: Oxygen prongs ke nishaan kaan ke peeche aur naak par roz dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every place where a device presses is examined for the skin beneath.

question: A nurse is to take a 65-year-old man on the ward who has a urinary catheter to another room in a wheel chair. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Empty the bag before the move and leave the catheter open to the air
option_2: Hang the urine bag on the back of the chair above the level of the bladder
option_3: Ask the man to hold the urine bag in his lap during the move
option_4: Put the urine bag below the level of the bladder and keep it off the floor
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Put the urine bag below the level of the bladder and keep it off the floor

Clinical Rationale: The bag is put below the level of the bladder and kept off the floor during the move, so that the urine does NOT run back into the bladder.

Key Clue: 65-year-old man with a urinary catheter to be taken in a wheel chair to another room

Priority Principle: Safety / Urine bag

Why Not Others: (a) A catheter left open to the air takes the germs of the room; (b) A bag above the bladder on the back of the chair lets the urine run back; (c) A bag in the lap pulls at the tube and wets the clothes.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the back of the chair seems the easy place for the bag.

5-Second Recall: Move ke waqt bag bladder se neeche aur farsh se oopar rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The bag stays below the bladder at every move of the client.

question: A nurse must give skin care round the tracheostomy tube of a 50-year-old man on the ward who has a fresh tube, and the nurse notes that the skin under the flange is red. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the skin, keep it dry and check the ties and the press of the tube
option_2: Put a thick gauze under the flange and press the tube down well
option_3: Loosen the ties and take the tube out to see the skin under it
option_4: Put a powder on the skin and leave the tube as it is
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the skin, keep it dry and check the ties and the press of the tube

Clinical Rationale: Red skin under the flange of a tracheostomy tube is cleaned and kept dry and the ties and the press are checked, because a press that stays for days brings a sore and an infection.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man with a fresh tracheostomy tube and red skin under the flange

Priority Principle: Skin safety / Tracheostomy tube

Why Not Others: (b) A thick gauze and a press of the tube make the skin under it worse; (c) A tube taken out for a look at the skin risks the airway; (d) A powder under the flange holds the damp and the germs.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a thick gauze seems the guard of the skin.

5-Second Recall: Tracheostomy flange ke neeche laali = skin saaf-sukhi karo, tie aur press check karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The ties of a tracheostomy are tight enough for one finger and no more.

question: A nurse on the ward finds the family of a 65-year-old man who has a nasogastric tube for feeding giving him a glass of milk from home. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Allow a small amount of milk and note it against the feed of the hour
option_2: Stop the milk at once and tell the family that nothing goes by the mouth with the tube
option_3: Ask the family to give the milk by the tube with a syringe
option_4: Note the milk in the chart and give the feed at the usual hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the milk at once and tell the family that nothing goes by the mouth with the tube

Clinical Rationale: The milk is stopped at once and the family is told that the mouth takes nothing while the tube is in place, so that the feed does NOT enter the lungs.

Key Clue: family of a 65-year-old man with a nasogastric tube giving him a glass of milk from home

Priority Principle: Safety / Nasogastric tube

Why Not Others: (a) A small amount of milk by the mouth can still enter the airway; (c) Milk given by the family down the tube is not ordered and not measured; (d) A feed after the milk by the mouth gives too much of the fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a small amount of milk seems the kind wish of a family.

5-Second Recall: Tube wale client ko muh se kuch nahi - parivar ko samjhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The order of nothing by mouth is told to the family in simple words.

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward has a drip needle in a vein of the foot, and the nurse must keep the leg in the right position. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Put the leg under the knee with a firm pillow
option_2: Move the foot up and down many times so that the fluid runs
option_3: Keep the leg straight and still and call the nurse if the site pains
option_4: Take a walk to the toilet with the bottle of the drip in the hand
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the leg straight and still and call the nurse if the site pains

Clinical Rationale: A needle in a vein of the foot needs the leg straight and still with a call to the nurse at any pain, so that the needle does NOT come out of the vein.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man with a drip needle in a vein of the foot

Priority Principle: Safety / Drip line

Why Not Others: (a) A pillow under the knee bends the line and the vein; (b) Moving the foot up and down pushes the needle through the vein; (d) A walk with the bottle in the hand pulls the needle out of the foot.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a pillow under the knee seems the easy rest of a leg.

5-Second Recall: Pair ki nass me needle = pair seedha aur still rakho, dard par bell bajao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A needle in a vein of the foot is watched for pain and swelling.

question: A nurse reads the urine report of a 70-year-old man on the ward who has a urinary catheter, and the report names a germ with a list of the drugs that the germ is sensitive to. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the catheter out of the bladder so that the germ goes away
option_2: Empty the urine bag and note the amount for the day
option_3: Ask the family to buy the drug that heads the list of the report
option_4: Read the list with the doctor's order and inform the doctor about the germ
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Read the list with the doctor's order and inform the doctor about the germ

Clinical Rationale: The list of drugs on the report is read with the doctor's order and the germ is told to the doctor, so that the right drug is chosen for the man.

Key Clue: urine report of a 70-year-old man with a urinary catheter naming a germ and a list of drugs

Priority Principle: Lab / Urine report

Why Not Others: (a) A catheter taken out before the drug may leave the bladder without a way out; (b) Emptying the bag says nothing of the germ and the drug; (c) A drug bought by the family is not the doctor's order.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the FIRST drug of the list seems the drug that must be bought.

5-Second Recall: Urine culture report = doctor ke order se milao, germ ki khabar do.

PNC Exam Pearl: A culture report is read with the order before any drug is started.
